Correlational analysis of the relationship between attention and choice in a
2-attribute binary choice task where attributes can be positive (P), negative
(N), or ambivalent (B). Study 1 (PAS3) and Study 2 (PAS4) use the same task;
Study 2 doubled the trials per participant and blocked trial types.

This notebook reads the merged data written by
`code/preprocessing/merge_PAS3_PAS4_to_main_data.R` and produces every figure
and regression table in the paper. Sections follow the order of the Results:

1. Basic psychometrics
2. Fixation properties
3. Option-level attention
4. Attribute-level attention
5. Range sensitivity

Figures are saved to `paper/figures/`, LaTeX tables to `paper/tables/`, and the
statistics quoted in the text of the paper to `paper/text_output/` (one small
.tex file each; see the "Text Output" subsections). The last section, "Extra
Analyses", holds analyses that are not in the paper and is switched off by
default.

# Preamble

```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(glmmTMB)       # frequentist logistic mixed models
library(lme4)          # frequentist linear mixed models
library(brms)          # Bayesian attention-weight and value-sensitivity models
library(bayestestR)    # highest density intervals
library(patchwork)     # combining ggplots into one figure
library(modelsummary)  # regression tables -> LaTeX

# Project utilities. This gives us the plot theme (.myPlot), the Narrow / Wide
# color and shape scales (.wn_colors, .wn_shapes), figure size defaults
# (.figw, .figh, .linewidth), and `paths`.
source(here::here("code/utilities/getAllUtilities.R"))
```

```{r options}
# Set to FALSE for a fast, figures-only pass. The attribute-level figure still
# gets drawn from the cached brms fits in notebooks/brm_fits/ and the cached
# held-out predictions of the Bayesian model. Set to TRUE to
# fit every regression, write the LaTeX tables and the in-text statistics, and
# sample any brms model whose cache is missing (the two attention-weight fits,
# Narrow and Wide, take many hours each the first time; see
# code/fitting/sample_pooled_attention_weights.R to run them from a terminal).
RUN_REGRESSIONS <- FALSE

# Where things live (absolute paths built from config/paths.yaml).
data_dir <- file.path(paths$root, paths$data$processed)
fig_dir  <- file.path(paths$root, paths$paper_figures)
tab_dir  <- file.path(paths$root, paths$paper_tables)
text_dir <- file.path(paths$root, paths$paper_text)
fit_dir  <- file.path(paths$root, paths$notebooks, "brm_fits")
# Caches of the Bayesian model (written by code/fitting/run_bayesian_fits.R).
bayes_dir <- file.path(paths$root, paths$results$cache, "bayesian_model")
for (d in c(fig_dir, tab_dir, text_dir, fit_dir)) dir.create(d, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# brms sampling settings (cmdstanr backend).
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
options(brms.backend = "cmdstanr")
BRMS_CHAINS <- 4
BRMS_SEED   <- 1234

# Keep numbers in the LaTeX tables plain (no siunitx \num{} wrappers).
options("modelsummary_format_numeric_latex" = "plain")

# Weakly informative priors used by every brms model below.
brms_priors <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 2.5), class = "b"),
  prior(normal(0, 2),   class = "Intercept")
)
```

```{r plot-helpers}
# Layout conventions for every figure:
#   - Narrow vs Wide is shown with color AND marker shape (wn_scales below).
#   - Attribute type (N / B / P) is shown by faceting, so it needs no color.
#   - Study is a title over each half of a combined figure, or a facet strip in
#     figures that have no other faceting.
#   - Size: every figure is 2 * .figw wide and (number of rows) * .figh tall,
#     and all text sizes come from .tick_pt / .title_pt / .strip_pt in
#     MyPlotOptions.
study_labels <- as_labeller(c("1" = "Study 1", "2" = "Study 2"))
type_labels  <- as_labeller(c("N" = "Aversive (N)", "B" = "Ambivalent (B)", "P" = "Appetitive (P)"))

# Strips that say Study 1 / Study 2 (same look as the Study titles).
strip_style <- theme(
  strip.background = element_blank(),
  strip.text       = element_text(size = .title_pt * .fontscale, face = "bold")
)
# Strips that say Aversive / Ambivalent / Appetitive. Small and not bold so
# that all three fit on one line over a facet.
type_strip_style <- theme(
  strip.background = element_blank(),
  strip.text       = element_text(size = .strip_pt * .fontscale)
)
no_strip <- theme(strip.text = element_blank())

# Title over each study's half of a combined figure.
study_title <- theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = .title_pt * .fontscale))

# Narrow / Wide colors and markers. Both scales are named "Range", so ggplot
# merges them into a single legend.
wn_scales <- list(
  scale_color_manual(name = "Range", values = .wn_colors),
  scale_shape_manual(name = "Range", values = .wn_shapes)
)

# Nudge Narrow and Wide points apart slightly so they don't sit on top of each
# other (the two ranges share most of their x-values).
wn_dodge <- position_dodge(width = 2)

# x-axis ticks for the N / B / P facets, where x is an attribute value. At this
# text size, labeling every value ("-50 -40 -30 -20 -10") makes the labels run
# into each other, so we label every other value of the Wide range instead.
# With free x scales, ggplot calls this once per facet with that facet's limits.
x_attr_breaks <- function(limits) {
  if (limits[2] < 0) return(c(-50, -30, -10))   # aversive facet
  if (limits[1] > 0) return(c(10, 30, 50))      # appetitive facet
  c(-20, 0, 20)                                 # ambivalent facet
}

# Legends. .myPlot hides legends by default, so every plot with a Range legend
# turns it on with legend_bottom. In a combined figure, guide_area() at the
# bottom collects the identical legends into one centered legend. (The
# installed patchwork, 1.3.0, can't apply themes to a patchwork object under
# ggplot2 4.x, so we don't use `&` to set legend positions.)
legend_bottom <- theme(legend.position = "bottom")
legend_right <- theme(legend.position = "right")

# Point and error-bar sizes for the means +/- SE in every figure. Fitted lines
# use .linewidth from MyPlotOptions.
pt_size      <- 0
pt_linewidth <- 0.7

# In a combined figure, a missing panel (e.g. a fit that was not run) leaves an
# empty space rather than breaking the layout: get_or_spacer(panels, "Data").
get_or_spacer <- function(plots, key) {
  if (is.null(plots[[key]])) plot_spacer() else plots[[key]]
}
```

```{r model-helpers}
# Load a cached brms fit if it exists. If it doesn't, fit it only when
# RUN_REGRESSIONS is TRUE; otherwise return NULL so the plotting code can skip
# that panel. brm() itself does the caching through its `file` argument.
load_or_fit <- function(name, ...) {
  file <- file.path(fit_dir, name)
  if (!file.exists(paste0(file, ".rds")) && !RUN_REGRESSIONS) {
    cat("No cached fit for", name, "and RUN_REGRESSIONS is FALSE. Skipping.\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  brm(..., file = file)
}

# Regression tables. Every regression crosses its predictors with range
# (WNWide) and study (Study2), so each predictor has four coefficients: its
# value at the reference levels (Narrow, Study 1) and its interactions with
# Wide, with Study 2, and with both. Listed as rows, those ran the tables off
# the page, so each predictor gets one row and its four coefficients go in
# four columns. The column headers, keyed by moderator:
range_study_columns <- c("ref"           = "Narrow, Study 1",
                         "WNWide"        = "× Wide",
                         "Study2"        = "× Study 2",
                         "WNWide:Study2" = "× Wide × Study 2")
# The attention-weight models are fit within one range, so they only have study.
study_columns <- c("ref" = "Study 1", "Study2" = "× Study 2")

# Split coefficient names such as "Diff10:WNWide:Study2" into the predictor
# ("Diff10") and its moderators ("WNWide:Study2"). A coefficient with no
# moderator gets "ref"; a moderator on its own (e.g. "WNWide") is the
# intercept's interaction.
split_moderators <- function(term) {
  out <- tibble()
  for (tm in term) {
    pieces <- str_split(tm, ":")[[1]]
    is_mod <- pieces %in% c("WNWide", "Study2")
    out <- bind_rows(out, tibble(
      predictor = if (all(is_mod)) "(Intercept)" else paste(pieces[!is_mod], collapse = ":"),
      moderator = if (any(is_mod)) paste(pieces[is_mod], collapse = ":") else "ref"
    ))
  }
  out
}

# Readable names for the predictors. Values are in units of 10 points and
# dwell times in seconds.
term_labels <- c(
  "(Intercept)"    = "Intercept",
  "Intercept"      = "Intercept",        # brms spells it without parentheses
  "Diff10"         = "Value Diff.",      # left minus right
  "Difficulty10"   = "Abs. Value Diff.", # best minus worst
  "DwellDiff"      = "Net Dwell",        # left minus right
  "RelDiff10_last" = "Value Diff.",      # last-fixated minus other option
  "LastTypeN"      = "Last N",
  "LastTypeB"      = "Last B",
  "fix_typeN"      = "Type N",
  "fix_typeB"      = "Type B",
  "fix_value10"    = "Value",
  "typeN"          = "Type N",
  "typeB"          = "Type B",
  "value10"        = "Value",
  "SV_P"           = "Value Diff. (P)",
  "SV_N"           = "Value Diff. (N)",
  "SV_B"           = "Value Diff. (B)",
  "S2"             = "Study 2"          # Study 2 term on the intercept (pooled attention-weight models)
)

# Label predictors with term_labels, piece by piece for interactions
# ("Diff10:DwellDiff" -> "Value Diff. × Net Dwell"). Attention-weight cells
# read like the figures ("N_neg50" -> "N, -50"), and so do their utilities
# ("U_N_neg50" -> "N, -50"). Anything else passes through.
label_term <- function(term) {
  labels <- c()
  for (tm in term) {
    pieces <- str_split(tm, ":")[[1]]
    for (k in seq_along(pieces)) {
      cell <- str_remove(pieces[k], "^U_")   # a utility is labeled like its cell
      if (pieces[k] %in% names(term_labels)) {
        pieces[k] <- term_labels[[pieces[k]]]
      } else if (str_detect(cell, "^[PNB]_(neg|pos)[0-9]+$")) {
        sign <- if (str_detect(cell, "_neg")) "-" else ""
        pieces[k] <- paste0(str_sub(cell, 1, 1), ", ", sign, str_extract(cell, "[0-9]+$"))
      }
    }
    labels <- c(labels, paste(pieces, collapse = " × "))
  }
  labels
}

# Fixed effects of an lme4 or glmmTMB fit with 95% Wald CIs.
tidy_freq <- function(fit) {
  get_estimates(fit) %>%
    filter(effect == "fixed") %>%
    select(term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high)
}

# Random-effect SDs of an lme4 or glmmTMB fit, named by predictor. modelsummary
# calls them "SD (Diff10 Subject)", and the residual SD of a linear model
# "SD (Observations)".
sds_freq <- function(fit) {
  re  <- get_estimates(fit) %>% filter(str_detect(term, "^SD \\("))
  nms <- re$term %>%
    str_remove("^SD \\(") %>%
    str_remove(" Subject\\)$") %>%
    str_replace("^Observations\\)$", "Residual")
  setNames(re$estimate, nms)
}

# Fit statistics for the bottom of a table: number of trials, marginal and
# conditional R2 (Nakagawa's, as computed by modelsummary through the
# performance package), and how the model was estimated ("Frequentist (lme4)").
gof_freq <- function(fit, estimation) {
  g <- get_gof(fit)
  tibble(
    nobs           = g$nobs,
    r2.marginal    = if (is.null(g$r2.marginal))    NA_real_ else g$r2.marginal,
    r2.conditional = if (is.null(g$r2.conditional)) NA_real_ else g$r2.conditional,
    estimation     = estimation
  )
}

# One model as the columns of a regression table: a modelsummary_list per
# moderator in `columns`, holding that moderator's coefficient for every
# predictor (the rows). The fit statistics go under the first column only.
# Numbers are formatted here, to `digits` decimals, so that one panel of a
# table can show more decimals than another.
table_columns <- function(coefs, gof, columns, digits = 3) {
  coefs <- bind_cols(coefs, split_moderators(coefs$term))
  # `+ 0` turns a rounded negative zero into a plain zero ("0.000", not "-0.000").
  # A missing bound stays missing: a row fixed by construction has no interval.
  fmt   <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), NA_character_, formatC(round(x, digits) + 0, format = "f", digits = digits))

  out <- list()
  for (m in names(columns)) {
    rows <- coefs %>% filter(moderator == m)
    tidy <- tibble(
      term      = label_term(rows$predictor),
      estimate  = fmt(rows$estimate),
      conf.low  = fmt(rows$conf.low),
      conf.high = fmt(rows$conf.high)
    )
    # A `text` column in coefs prints verbatim in place of the estimate, e.g.
    # "0 (reference)" for a utility that is fixed at zero by construction.
    if ("text" %in% names(rows)) tidy$estimate[!is.na(rows$text)] <- rows$text[!is.na(rows$text)]
    glance <- if (m == names(columns)[1]) gof else tibble(nobs = NA_real_)
    out[[columns[[m]]]] <- structure(list(tidy = tidy, glance = glance), class = "modelsummary_list")
  }
  out
}

# The same for an lme4 / glmmTMB fit crossed with range and study, which is
# every frequentist model in the paper.
freq_columns <- function(fit, estimation, digits = 3) {
  table_columns(tidy_freq(fit), gof_freq(fit, estimation), range_study_columns, digits)
}

# Table note with the random-effect SDs. `sds` is a list with one named vector
# per panel (from sds_freq or sds_brms), named by panel ("Panel A") or unnamed
# for a table with one model. Entries are separated by semicolons because cell
# labels ("N, -30") have commas in them.
sd_note <- function(sds, intro = "Random-effect SDs across subjects.") {
  parts <- c()
  for (p in seq_along(sds)) {
    x       <- sds[[p]]
    entries <- paste(label_term(names(x)), formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3), collapse = "; ")
    panel   <- names(sds)[p]
    if (is.null(panel) || panel == "") {
      parts <- c(parts, paste0(entries, "."))
    } else {
      parts <- c(parts, paste0(panel, ": ", entries, "."))
    }
  }
  paste("\\textit{Note.}", intro, paste(parts, collapse = " "))
}

# Write a regression table to paper/tables/<name>.tex as a booktabs tabular
# plus an optional note under it (so it can be \input into a table environment
# in the paper), and echo the LaTeX so it also shows up in the knitted
# notebook. `tab` is either one model's columns (from table_columns) or a named
# list of them, one per panel ("Panel A: Choice" = ...), which modelsummary
# stacks with shape = "rbind". Intervals go on a line of their own under each
# estimate, unless `ci_inline` is TRUE, which puts them next to the estimate
# (halving the length of a table that has room to spare in width).
# `coef_order` (row labels, in order) fixes the row order when the models in a
# table have different rows; otherwise rows follow their first appearance.
save_tex <- function(tab, name, note = NULL, ci_inline = FALSE, coef_order = NULL) {
  file      <- file.path(tab_dir, paste0(name, ".tex"))
  coef_map  <- if (is.null(coef_order)) NULL else setNames(coef_order, coef_order)
  is_panels <- !inherits(tab[[1]], "modelsummary_list")
  if (ci_inline) {
    # Put the interval next to the estimate here rather than through
    # modelsummary's glue template, so that a row without an interval (a
    # reference fixed at zero) prints its estimate alone.
    inline <- function(m) {
      t      <- m$tidy
      has_ci <- !is.na(t$conf.low) & !is.na(t$conf.high)
      t$estimate <- ifelse(has_ci, paste0(t$estimate, " [", t$conf.low, ", ", t$conf.high, "]"), t$estimate)
      m$tidy <- t %>% select(-conf.low, -conf.high)
      m
    }
    if (is_panels) {
      for (p in seq_along(tab)) for (k in seq_along(tab[[p]])) tab[[p]][[k]] <- inline(tab[[p]][[k]])
    } else {
      for (k in seq_along(tab)) tab[[k]] <- inline(tab[[k]])
    }
    estimate  <- "{estimate}"
    statistic <- NULL
  } else {
    estimate  <- "{estimate}"
    statistic <- "conf.int"
  }

  # The only fit statistics we report (in this order). "estimation" is the
  # label from gof_freq / gof_brms, so the reader can tell which models were
  # fit by maximum likelihood and which by MCMC.
  gof_map <- list(
    list(raw = "nobs",           clean = "Num.Obs.",   fmt = 0),
    list(raw = "r2.marginal",    clean = "R2 Marg.",   fmt = 3),
    list(raw = "r2.conditional", clean = "R2 Cond.",   fmt = 3),
    list(raw = "estimation",     clean = "Estimation", fmt = identity)
  )
  if (is_panels) {
    tex <- modelsummary(tab, shape = "rbind", estimate = estimate, statistic = statistic,
                        gof_map = gof_map, coef_map = coef_map, output = "latex_tabular")
  } else {
    tex <- modelsummary(tab, estimate = estimate, statistic = statistic,
                        gof_map = gof_map, coef_map = coef_map, output = "latex_tabular")
  }
  tex   <- strsplit(paste(as.character(tex), collapse = "\n"), "\n")[[1]]
  n_col <- nchar(str_match(tex[1], "\\{(l+)\\}")[, 2])

  # modelsummary's bare tabular has no horizontal rules and writes a panel's
  # title into every column. Go through it line by line and add the usual
  # booktabs rules, one title per panel, and a single Estimation label per
  # model spread over all the coefficient columns.
  out <- c()
  for (i in seq_along(tex)) {
    line  <- tex[i]
    cells <- str_trim(str_split(str_remove(str_trim(line), "\\\\\\\\$"), "&")[[1]])
    if (str_detect(line, "^\\\\begin\\{tabular\\}")) {
      out <- c(out, line, "\\toprule")
    } else if (i == 2) {
      # the header; a panel title below it brings its own rule
      out <- c(out, line)
      if (!is_panels) out <- c(out, "\\midrule")
    } else if (str_detect(line, "^\\\\end\\{tabular\\}")) {
      out <- c(out, "\\bottomrule", line)
    } else if (length(cells) == n_col && cells[1] != "" && all(cells == cells[1])) {
      out <- c(out, "\\midrule", paste0("\\multicolumn{", n_col, "}{l}{\\textit{", cells[1], "}} \\\\"))
    } else if (str_detect(line, "^Num.Obs.")) {
      out <- c(out, if (is_panels) "\\addlinespace" else "\\midrule", line)
    } else if (str_detect(line, "^R2 ")) {
      out <- c(out, paste0("$R^2$", str_remove(line, "^R2")))
    } else if (str_detect(line, "^Estimation")) {
      out <- c(out, paste0("Estimation & \\multicolumn{", n_col - 1, "}{l}{", cells[2], "} \\\\"))
    } else {
      out <- c(out, line)
    }
  }

  # The note spans the text width, in script size, under the table.
  if (!is.null(note)) {
    out <- c(out, "\\par\\medskip",
             paste0("\\begin{minipage}{\\linewidth}\\scriptsize ", note, "\\end{minipage}"))
  }

  writeLines(out, file)
  cat(out, sep = "\n")
}

# Population-level effects of a brms fit as a tidy table: posterior median and
# 95% HDI for every b_ parameter (the "b_" prefix is dropped from the names).
tidy_brms <- function(fit) {
  draws <- as_draws_df(fit, variable = "^b_", regex = TRUE)
  pars  <- grep("^b_", names(draws), value = TRUE)

  out <- tibble()
  for (par in pars) {
    x <- draws[[par]]
    h <- bayestestR::hdi(x, ci = 0.95)
    out <- bind_rows(out, tibble(
      term = str_remove(par, "^b_"), estimate = median(x),
      conf.low = h$CI_low, conf.high = h$CI_high
    ))
  }
  out
}

# Posterior medians of the subject-level SDs of a brms fit, named by predictor
# like sds_freq ("sd_Subject__SV_P" -> "SV_P").
sds_brms <- function(fit) {
  draws <- as_draws_df(fit, variable = "^sd_", regex = TRUE)
  pars  <- grep("^sd_", names(draws), value = TRUE)
  sds   <- c()
  for (par in pars) {
    sds[str_remove(par, "^sd_Subject__")] <- median(draws[[par]])
  }
  sds[cell_order(names(sds))]   # same order as the table rows
}

# Fit statistics of a brms fit, like gof_freq. modelsummary would compute LOO
# for these big fits, which takes forever, so we compute the Bayesian R2
# ourselves: conditional on the subject effects, and marginal (without them).
# 1,000 evenly spaced posterior draws are plenty for a median.
gof_brms <- function(fit, estimation = "Bayesian (brms)") {
  ids <- round(seq(1, ndraws(fit), length.out = 1000))
  tibble(
    nobs           = nrow(fit$data),
    r2.marginal    = median(bayes_R2(fit, re_formula = NA, summary = FALSE, draw_ids = ids)),
    r2.conditional = median(bayes_R2(fit, summary = FALSE, draw_ids = ids)),
    estimation     = estimation
  )
}

# Order for the attention-weight tables: the intercept and other predictors
# as they come, then the cells sorted like the figures, by type (N, B, P) and
# then by value. `pred` are predictor names such as "SV_P", "N_neg50" or
# "U_N_neg50" (a utility sorts like its cell).
cell_order <- function(pred) {
  pred    <- str_remove(pred, "^U_")
  is_cell <- str_detect(pred, "^[PNB]_(neg|pos)[0-9]+$")
  type    <- match(str_sub(pred, 1, 1), c("N", "B", "P"))
  value   <- as.numeric(str_extract(pred, "[0-9]+$")) * if_else(str_detect(pred, "_neg"), -1, 1)
  # order() is stable, so the non-cells (all ties here) keep their order
  order(is_cell, ifelse(is_cell, type, 0), ifelse(is_cell, value, 0))
}

# Rows of a tidy coefficient table in that order.
order_cells <- function(coefs) {
  coefs[cell_order(split_moderators(coefs$term)$predictor), ]
}
```

```{r text-helpers}
# Statistics quoted in the text of the paper. Each one is a short LaTeX math
# snippet saved to paper/text_output/<name>.tex, which main.tex pulls in with
# \input{text_output/<name>} in place of the numbers. write.text() (from
# code/utilities) writes the string with no trailing newline, so \input adds
# no stray space inside a parenthesis.
# Notation: the study (or a contrast between studies) is always the subscript;
# the superscript is for everything else (attribute type, range, predictor...).
save_text <- function(text, name) {
  write.text(text, file.path(text_dir, paste0(name, ".tex")))
  cat(text, "\n")
}

# "0.013\ [0.003, 0.023]": an estimate with its 95% interval.
fmt_ci <- function(est, lo, hi, digits = 3) {
  z <- function(x) round(x, digits) + 0   # so a bound that rounds to 0 prints as 0.000, not -0.000
  sprintf("%.*f\\ [%.*f, %.*f]", digits, z(est), digits, z(lo), digits, z(hi))
}

# p-values: three decimals, or scientific notation below .001 (e.g. "p = 3e-15").
fmt_p <- function(p) {
  if (p < 0.001) paste0("p = ", formatC(p, format = "e", digits = 0)) else sprintf("p = %.3f", p)
}

# Estimate and 95% Wald CI of a linear combination of fixed effects, e.g. the
# Study 2 slope = b_slope + b_slope:Study2. `terms` are coefficient names and
# `weights` their multipliers (by default they are just added up). lmer
# returns fixef() and vcov() directly; glmmTMB wraps them in a list with a
# $cond element. With tens of thousands of trials the 1.96 normal cutoff gives
# the same intervals as the tables (to three decimals).
coef_ci <- function(fit, terms, weights = rep(1, length(terms))) {
  b <- fixef(fit); if (is.list(b)) b <- b$cond
  V <- vcov(fit);  if (is.list(V)) V <- V$cond
  V <- as.matrix(V)
  est <- sum(weights * b[terms])
  se  <- sqrt(as.numeric(t(weights) %*% V[terms, terms] %*% weights))
  c(estimate = est, lo = est - 1.96 * se, hi = est + 1.96 * se)
}

# The same, already formatted, so one snippet is one line of code.
fmt_coef <- function(fit, terms, weights = rep(1, length(terms)), digits = 3) {
  ci <- coef_ci(fit, terms, weights)
  fmt_ci(ci[["estimate"]], ci[["lo"]], ci[["hi"]], digits)
}

# Posterior median and 95% HDI of a vector of draws, formatted like fmt_ci.
fmt_post <- function(draws, digits = 3) {
  h <- bayestestR::hdi(draws, ci = 0.95)
  fmt_ci(median(draws), h$CI_low, h$CI_high, digits)
}

# t-test between two vectors of subject means, in the format
# "$\Delta^{sup}_{sub} = 2.59$, $d = 0.39$, $t(1298.3) = 7.1$, $p = 2e-12$",
# where `sup` says what is compared (e.g. "\\text{Wide - Narrow}") and `sub`
# the study (e.g. "Study 1"; left out if NULL). Welch's test by default;
# paired = TRUE when both vectors come from the same subjects in the same
# order. Cohen's d uses the pooled SD (Welch) or the SD of the paired
# differences. `unit` is appended to Delta (e.g. "\\ \\text{s}").
fmt_ttest <- function(x, y, sup, sub = NULL, unit = "", paired = FALSE, digits = 2) {
  tt    <- t.test(x, y, paired = paired)
  delta <- mean(x) - mean(y)
  if (paired) {
    d <- delta / sd(x - y)
  } else {
    sp <- sqrt(((length(x) - 1) * var(x) + (length(y) - 1) * var(y)) / (length(x) + length(y) - 2))
    d  <- delta / sp
  }
  df   <- tt$parameter
  df   <- if (df == round(df)) sprintf("%d", df) else sprintf("%.1f", df)   # paired tests: whole df
  name <- paste0("\\Delta^{", sup, "}", if (!is.null(sub)) paste0("_{\\text{", sub, "}}"))
  sprintf("$%s = %.*f%s$, $d = %.2f$, $t(%s) = %.1f$, $%s$",
          name, digits, delta, unit, d, df, tt$statistic, fmt_p(tt$p.value))
}
```

# Data

```{r read-data}
pas_raw  <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "main_data.csv"),      show_col_types = FALSE)
long_raw <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "main_data_long.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Trial level

One row per trial. `Subject` is already unique across studies (e.g. "S1_5" vs
"S2_5"), so it can be used directly as the grouping variable everywhere.

```{r clean-trial}
pas <- pas_raw %>%
  mutate(
    WN      = factor(WN,  levels = c("Narrow", "Wide")),   # Narrow is the reference level
    BPN     = factor(BPN, levels = c("PN", "PB", "NB")),
    ChooseL = as.integer(ChooseL),                         # TRUE/FALSE -> 1/0
    Correct = as.integer(Correct),
    Difficulty = abs(Diff),                                # best minus worst option value
    # Regressions use value in units of 10 points, matching the paper's SV_* convention.
    Diff10       = Diff / 10,
    Difficulty10 = Difficulty / 10
  )
```

## Box level

Each trial has four boxes (left/right option x top/bottom attribute). Stack them
so there is one row per box, with the box's attribute type, value, and dwell
time. Left boxes get a side sign of +1 (looking there should push choice toward
"left"), right boxes -1.

```{r boxlong}
mk_box <- function(df, box, side_sign, type_col, val_col, dwell_col) {
  df %>%
    transmute(
      Study, Subject, Trial, WN, ChooseL,
      box       = box,
      side_sign = side_sign,
      type      = .data[[type_col]],
      value     = .data[[val_col]],
      dwell     = .data[[dwell_col]]
    )
}

boxlong <- bind_rows(
  mk_box(pas, "LT",  1, "AttT", "VLT", "DwellLT"),
  mk_box(pas, "LB",  1, "AttB", "VLB", "DwellLB"),
  mk_box(pas, "RT", -1, "AttT", "VRT", "DwellRT"),
  mk_box(pas, "RB", -1, "AttB", "VRB", "DwellRB")
) %>%
  mutate(
    type = factor(type, levels = c("P", "N", "B")),
    # Signed dwell: seconds, positive if it should push choice toward this box's side.
    signed_dwell = side_sign * dwell,
    # Signed value, in units of 10 points.
    signed_value = side_sign * value / 10,
    # Cell label for (type x value), e.g. "N_neg10", "P_pos5". Used to name the
    # attention-weight coefficients.
    cell = paste0(type, "_", if_else(value < 0, "neg", "pos"), abs(value))
  )
```

## Fixation level

One row per fixation (mouse hover). `FixDur` is in ms. Tag each fixation with
the value and type of the box it landed on.

```{r clean-long}
long <- long_raw %>%
  mutate(
    WN = factor(WN, levels = c("Narrow", "Wide")),
    fix_value = case_when(
      FixROI == "LT" ~ VLT, FixROI == "RT" ~ VRT,
      FixROI == "LB" ~ VLB, FixROI == "RB" ~ VRB
    ),
    fix_value10 = fix_value / 10,
    fix_type = factor(if_else(FixROI %in% c("LT", "RT"), AttT, AttB),
                      levels = c("P", "N", "B")),
    fix_side = if_else(FixROI %in% c("LT", "LB"), "L", "R")
  )
```

### First and last fixation of each trial

Needed for the first-fixation and last-fixation analyses. Trials with no
fixation record (about 500 per study) get NA here and drop out of those
analyses.

```{r first-last}
first_last <- long %>%
  arrange(Study, Subject, Trial, FixNum) %>%
  group_by(Study, Subject, Trial) %>%
  summarise(
    FirstSide = first(fix_side),
    LastSide  = last(fix_side),
    LastType  = last(fix_type),
    .groups   = "drop"
  )

pas <- pas %>%
  left_join(first_last, by = c("Study", "Subject", "Trial")) %>%
  mutate(
    # Was the first fixation to the better option? Undefined when the options tie.
    BestSide     = case_when(Diff > 0 ~ "L", Diff < 0 ~ "R", TRUE ~ NA_character_),
    FirstFixBest = as.integer(FirstSide == BestSide),
    # Did the subject choose the option they looked at last?
    ChooseLast = as.integer((LastSide == "L") == (ChooseL == 1)),
    # Value difference from the point of view of the last-fixated option
    # (last-fixated option minus the other one).
    RelDiff_last   = if_else(LastSide == "L", VL - VR, VR - VL),
    RelDiff10_last = RelDiff_last / 10
  )
```

### Fixation counts per box

For the share-of-fixations analysis: how many of a trial's fixations went to
each box. Boxes that were never fixated get a count of 0.

```{r box-grid}
fix_counts <- long %>% count(Study, Subject, Trial, FixROI, name = "n_fix")
fix_total  <- long %>% count(Study, Subject, Trial, name = "n_trial")

box_grid <- boxlong %>%
  transmute(Study, Subject, Trial, WN, FixROI = box, type, value, value10 = value / 10) %>%
  left_join(fix_counts, by = c("Study", "Subject", "Trial", "FixROI")) %>%
  left_join(fix_total,  by = c("Study", "Subject", "Trial")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(n_trial)) %>%                 # trials with no fixation record drop out
  mutate(
    n_fix = replace_na(n_fix, 0L),
    share = n_fix / n_trial
  )
```

# Basic Psychometrics

Choice as a function of the value difference between options, and response
time as a function of difficulty (best minus worst option value). In every
figure, points are means across participants with standard errors (each
participant contributes one mean per x-value first, then we average over
participants).

```{r psych-choice}
pdata_choice <- pas %>%
  group_by(Study, Subject, WN, Diff) %>%
  summarise(y_subject = mean(ChooseL), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Study, WN, Diff) %>%
  summarise(y = mean(y_subject), se = sd(y_subject) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")

p_choice <- ggplot(pdata_choice, aes(x = Diff, y = y, color = WN, shape = WN)) +
  facet_wrap(~ Study, labeller = study_labels) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0,   linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se), size = pt_size, linewidth = .linewidth,
                  position = wn_dodge) +
  #stat_smooth(method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "binomial"), se = FALSE, linewidth = .linewidth) +
  wn_scales +
  labs(x = "Value Difference (L - R)", y = "Pr(Choose Left)") +
  .myPlot + strip_style + legend_right +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.5), labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1))
```

```{r psych-rt}
pdata_rt <- pas %>%
  group_by(Study, Subject, WN, Difficulty) %>%
  summarise(y_subject = mean(RT), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Study, WN, Difficulty) %>%
  summarise(y = mean(y_subject), se = sd(y_subject) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")

p_rt <- ggplot(pdata_rt, aes(x = Difficulty, y = y, color = WN, shape = WN)) +
  facet_wrap(~ Study, labeller = study_labels) +
  geom_line(linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se), size = pt_size, linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
  #stat_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = .linewidth) +
  wn_scales +
  labs(x = "Best - Worst Value", y = "Response Time (s)") +
  .myPlot + strip_style + no_strip + legend_right +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(4, 10))
```

```{r fig-psychometrics, fig.width=2 * .figw, fig.height=2 * .figh}
# 2 rows (choice, RT) x 2 columns (Study 1, Study 2).
fig_psych <- (p_choice / p_rt) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect")

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "basic_psychometrics.pdf"), fig_psych, width = 2 * .figw, height = 2 * .figh)
fig_psych
```

## Range Sensitivity Simulations

The paper argues that the lower value sensitivity of the Wide condition is what
models of value normalization predict (Supplementary "Range Sensitivity
Simulations"). Here we simulate choices from four such models on two
hypothetical studies built from our own trials, then run the same choice
regression on each simulated data set. Every model maps a box's objective value
$a$ to a subjective value $f(a)$ through the context of its attribute type, an
option's subjective value is the sum of its two boxes, and choice is a logit on
the left minus right subjective value. Each model lives in its own script under
`code/simulation/`, with the shared pieces (trial sets, participants, choice
rule) in `simulate_normalized_choices.R`:

- **Range normalization** (`simulate_range_normalization.R`):
  $f(a) = (a - \min) / (\max - \min)$, where min and max are the smallest and
  largest value the type takes in the participant's range condition.
- **Context divisive normalization** (`simulate_context_divisive_normalization.R`):
  $f(a) = a / (\sigma_h + \omega \, \overline{|a|})$, dividing by the mean
  magnitude of the type's values in the range condition ($\sigma_h = 5$,
  $\omega = 1$).
- **Trial divisive normalization** (`simulate_trial_divisive_normalization.R`):
  $f(a_L) = a_L / (\sigma_h + \omega (|a_L| + |a_R|))$, dividing by the two
  values the attribute takes on the current trial (same parameters).
- **Rank normalization** (`simulate_rank_normalization.R`):
  $f(a) = (\text{rank}(a) - 1) / 5$, the rank of the value among the six
  values of its type in the range condition.

Each hypothetical study is one range condition with 60 real trials (20 per
block type, drawn from both studies) and 260 participants, matching Study 2.
Participants differ only in inverse temperature (uniform from 1 to 5); there
is no side bias, nothing about a participant depends on their condition, and
all four models use the same participants, trials, and random draws. Because
every participant sees the same 60 trials, a value difference that occurs on
only one or two trials reflects the makeup of those trials, which is why the
curves of the two divisive models are jagged.

```{r range-sim-simulate}
source(here::here("code/simulation/simulate_range_normalization.R"))
source(here::here("code/simulation/simulate_context_divisive_normalization.R"))
source(here::here("code/simulation/simulate_trial_divisive_normalization.R"))
source(here::here("code/simulation/simulate_rank_normalization.R"))

sim_design       <- design_values(pas)       # the six values per type and condition
sim_trials       <- make_trial_sets(pas)     # 60 real trials per condition
sim_participants <- draw_participants()      # 260 per condition

# One simulation function per model, named as the figure will label them.
sim_models <- list(
  "Range Normalization"            = simulate_range_normalization,
  "Context Divisive Normalization" = simulate_context_divisive_normalization,
  "Trial Divisive Normalization"   = simulate_trial_divisive_normalization,
  "Rank Normalization"             = simulate_rank_normalization
)

sim_data <- list()
for (m in names(sim_models)) {
  sim_data[[m]] <- sim_models[[m]](sim_trials, sim_participants, sim_design) %>% mutate(Model = m)
}
sim_data <- bind_rows(sim_data) %>% mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = names(sim_models)))
```

The regression is the choice model of the Regressions section below without the
study terms. The quantity of interest is the `Diff10:WNWide` interaction, the
Wide minus Narrow difference in slope. Each panel is annotated with the
condition that has the steeper slope and the p-value of that difference,
rounded to three decimals (in scientific notation when it is below .001). These four fits take a few seconds, so they run on every pass.

```{r range-sim-regressions}
sim_stats <- data.frame()
for (m in names(sim_models)) {
  fit <- glmmTMB(ChooseL ~ Diff10 * WN + (1 + Diff10 | Subject),
                 data = filter(sim_data, Model == m), family = binomial)
  coefs <- summary(fit)$coefficients$cond
  sim_stats <- rbind(sim_stats, data.frame(
    Model        = m,
    slope_narrow = coefs["Diff10", "Estimate"],
    slope_wide   = coefs["Diff10", "Estimate"] + coefs["Diff10:WNWide", "Estimate"],
    interaction  = coefs["Diff10:WNWide", "Estimate"],
    se           = coefs["Diff10:WNWide", "Std. Error"],
    p            = coefs["Diff10:WNWide", "Pr(>|z|)"]
  ))
}
# Annotation in the figure: which condition is steeper, and the p-value of the
# difference in slope (the Diff10:WNWide interaction). fmt_p (text-helpers)
# gives three decimals, or scientific notation when p is below .001 and three
# decimals would read 0.000 (e.g. "p = 8e-15"). All four models have a steeper
# Narrow slope; the direction word follows the sign of the interaction so that
# a label can never state the wrong direction.
sim_stats$label <- NA_character_
for (i in 1:nrow(sim_stats)) {
  steeper <- ifelse(sim_stats$interaction[i] < 0, "Narrow steeper than Wide", "Wide steeper than Narrow")
  sim_stats$label[i] <- paste0(steeper, " (", fmt_p(sim_stats$p[i]), ")")
}
sim_stats$Model <- factor(sim_stats$Model, levels = names(sim_models))
sim_stats
```

```{r fig-range-sim, fig.width=2 * .figw, fig.height=2 * .figh}
# 2 x 2 panels, one per model, formatted like the choice row of the basic
# psychometrics figure. Points are means across simulated participants with
# standard errors; the annotation in the bottom right of each panel says which
# condition is steeper and the p-value of the difference in slope.
pdata_sim <- sim_data %>%
  group_by(Model, Subject, WN, Diff) %>%
  summarise(y_subject = mean(ChooseL), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Model, WN, Diff) %>%
  summarise(y = mean(y_subject), se = sd(y_subject) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")

fig_range_sim <- ggplot(pdata_sim, aes(x = Diff, y = y, color = WN, shape = WN)) +
  facet_wrap(~ Model, ncol = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0,   linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se), size = pt_size, linewidth = .linewidth,
                  position = wn_dodge) +
  geom_text(data = sim_stats, aes(x = Inf, y = -Inf, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.6, size = .strip_pt * .fontscale / .pt) +
  wn_scales +
  labs(x = "Value Difference (L - R)", y = "Pr(Choose Left)") +
  .myPlot + strip_style + legend_right +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.5), labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1))

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "range_sensitivity_simulations.pdf"), fig_range_sim, width = 2 * .figw, height = 2 * .figh)
fig_range_sim
```

## Regressions

One model per outcome, pooled across both studies. Choice on value difference,
and RT on difficulty, each interacted with range and with study. Study 1 and
Narrow are the reference levels, so a `Study2` term is the Study 2 minus
Study 1 difference (at Narrow) and a `WNWide` term is the Wide minus Narrow
difference (in Study 1); the Study 2 version of any effect is the Study 1
coefficient plus its `:Study2` interaction. Random intercepts and slopes by
subject. In the RT model the intercept-slope correlation went to -1 when
estimated (a singular fit), so those random effects are uncorrelated.

```{r psych-regressions}
if (RUN_REGRESSIONS) {
  d <- pas %>% mutate(Study = factor(Study))   # 1 / 2 -> "1" / "2", reference "1"

  fit_choice <- glmmTMB(
    ChooseL ~ Diff10 * WN * Study + (1 + Diff10 | Subject),
    data = d, family = binomial
  )

  fit_rt <- lmer(
    RT ~ Difficulty10 * WN * Study + (1 + Difficulty10 || Subject),
    data = d, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  )

  # One panel per model, with the random-effect SDs in the note.
  tab <- list(
    "Panel A: Choice" = freq_columns(fit_choice, "Frequentist (glmmTMB)"),
    "Panel B: RT"     = freq_columns(fit_rt,     "Frequentist (lme4)")
  )
  note <- sd_note(list("Panel A" = sds_freq(fit_choice), "Panel B" = sds_freq(fit_rt)))
  save_tex(tab, "basic_psychometrics", note)
}
```

## Text Output

The statistics quoted in the Basic Psychometrics paragraph of the paper, one
chunk per snippet (see `save_text` in the preamble).

```{r text-rt-study-level}
if (RUN_REGRESSIONS) {
  # Study 2 minus Study 1 response time (s) from the pooled RT model. Study 1
  # and Narrow are the reference levels, so this is the difference at Narrow
  # and a value difference of 0.
  save_text(paste0("$\\Delta_{\\text{Study 2 - Study 1}} = ", fmt_coef(fit_rt, "Study2"), "\\ \\text{s}$"),
            "rt_study_level")
}
```

```{r text-rt-study-slope}
if (RUN_REGRESSIONS) {
  # Study 2 minus Study 1 difference in the RT slope on difficulty (s per 10
  # points): the Difficulty x Study interaction.
  save_text(paste0("$\\beta^{\\text{Difficulty}}_{\\text{Study 2 - Study 1}} = ", fmt_coef(fit_rt, "Difficulty10:Study2"), "$"),
            "rt_study_slope")
}
```

```{r text-rt-range-level}
if (RUN_REGRESSIONS) {
  # Wide minus Narrow response time (s) per study. WNWide is the Study 1
  # difference; Study 2 adds the WNWide:Study2 interaction.
  save_text(paste0(
    "$\\Delta^{\\text{Wide - Narrow}}_{\\text{Study 1}} = ", fmt_coef(fit_rt, "WNWide"), "$; ",
    "$\\Delta^{\\text{Wide - Narrow}}_{\\text{Study 2}} = ", fmt_coef(fit_rt, c("WNWide", "WNWide:Study2")), "$"
  ), "rt_range_level")
}
```

```{r text-rt-familiarity}
if (RUN_REGRESSIONS) {
  # Is Study 2 faster only because its subjects had more practice (60 trials
  # vs 30)? Mean RT per subject over a window of trial numbers. Picking by
  # trial number means trials dropped in preprocessing are missing the same
  # way in both studies.
  subj_rt <- function(s, trials) {
    pas %>%
      filter(Study == s, Trial %in% trials) %>%
      group_by(Subject) %>%
      summarise(rt = mean(RT), .groups = "drop") %>%
      pull(rt)
  }
  rt_s1       <- subj_rt(1, 1:30)   # all of Study 1
  rt_s2_early <- subj_rt(2, 1:30)
  rt_s2_late  <- subj_rt(2, 31:60)

  # Welch t-tests, Study 2 minus Study 1 (s): Study 2's later trials first,
  # then the trials where both studies had the same amount of practice.
  save_text(paste(
    fmt_ttest(rt_s2_late,  rt_s1, sup = "\\text{Trials 31--60 vs. 1--30}",
              sub = "Study 2 - Study 1", unit = "\\ \\text{s}"),
    fmt_ttest(rt_s2_early, rt_s1, sup = "\\text{Trials 1--30 vs. 1--30}",
              sub = "Study 2 - Study 1", unit = "\\ \\text{s}"),
    sep = "; "), "rt_familiarity")
}
```

# Fixation Properties

How attention was allocated before asking how it relates to choice: where the
first fixation went, how long individual fixations lasted, and how often each
box was revisited.

```{r fix-first}
# Pr(first fixation lands on the better option), by difficulty.
pdata_first <- pas %>%
  filter(!is.na(FirstFixBest)) %>%
  group_by(Study, Subject, WN, Difficulty) %>%
  summarise(y_subject = mean(FirstFixBest), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Study, WN, Difficulty) %>%
  summarise(y = mean(y_subject), se = sd(y_subject) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")

# One plot per study; the "Study s" title goes over each half of the combined
# figure. coord_cartesian() comes after .myPlot so that it isn't overwritten.
p_first <- list()
for (s in 1:2) {
  p_first[[s]] <- ggplot(pdata_first %>% filter(Study == s),
                         aes(x = Difficulty, y = y, color = WN, shape = WN)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50") +
    geom_line(linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se), size = pt_size, linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
    #stat_smooth(method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "binomial"), se = FALSE, linewidth = .linewidth) +
    wn_scales +
    labs(x = "Best - Worst Value", y = "Pr(First Fixation to Best)", title = paste("Study", s)) +
    .myPlot + strip_style + study_title + legend_right + theme(legend.direction = "vertical") +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1), xlim = c(0, 40)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.5), labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1))
}
```

```{r fix-duration}
# Mean duration of a single fixation, by the type and value of the fixated box.
# Facets are ordered N, B, P, like the attribute-level figure.
pdata_dur <- long %>%
  mutate(fix_type = factor(fix_type, levels = c("N", "B", "P"))) %>%
  group_by(Study, Subject, WN, fix_type, fix_value) %>%
  summarise(y_subject = mean(FixDur), .groups = "drop") %>%

p_dur <- list()
for (s in 1:2) {
  p_dur[[s]] <- ggplot(pdata_dur %>% filter(Study == s),
                       aes(x = fix_value, y = y, color = WN, shape = WN)) +
    facet_wrap(~ fix_type, scales = "free_x", labeller = type_labels) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se), size = pt_size, linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
    #stat_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = .linewidth) +
    wn_scales +
    labs(x = "Attribute Value", y = "Mean Fixation Duration (ms)") +
    .myPlot + type_strip_style + legend_right + theme(legend.direction = "vertical") +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(475, 850)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = x_attr_breaks) 
}
```

```{r fix-share}
# Share of a trial's fixations that went to a box, by its type and value.
# Under uniform attention every box would get 0.25.
pdata_share <- box_grid %>%
  mutate(type = factor(type, levels = c("N", "B", "P"))) %>%
  group_by(Study, Subject, WN, type, value) %>%
  summarise(y_subject = mean(share), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Study, WN, type, value) %>%
  summarise(y = mean(y_subject), se = sd(y_subject) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")

p_share <- list()
for (s in 1:2) {
  p_share[[s]] <- ggplot(pdata_share %>% filter(Study == s),
                         aes(x = value, y = y, color = WN, shape = WN)) +
    facet_wrap(~ type, scales = "free_x", labeller = type_labels) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0.25, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50") +
    geom_line(linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se), size = pt_size, linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
    #stat_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = .linewidth) +
    wn_scales +
    labs(x = "Attribute Value", y = "Mean Share of Fixations") +
    .myPlot + type_strip_style + legend_right + theme(legend.direction = "vertical") +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.2, 0.3)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.05), labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = x_attr_breaks)
}
```

## Regressions

One model per panel above, pooled across both studies with study crossed with
every other predictor (Study 1 and Narrow are the reference levels, as in the
psychometrics models). The first-fixation model uses uncorrelated random
effects for the same reason as the RT model (the correlation went to -1).
Fixation durations are right-skewed, so they are modeled on the log scale. The
share model is a linear mixed model on the plotted quantity (share of the
trial's fixations); this replaces the negative binomial count model from the
earlier notebooks, which had a degenerate dispersion estimate. Its subject
intercept variance is exactly zero by construction (every subject's shares
average to 0.25 across the four boxes), so lme4 reports a singular fit there;
the fixed effects are unaffected.

```{r fix-regressions}
if (RUN_REGRESSIONS) {
  d_trial <- pas      %>% filter(!is.na(FirstFixBest)) %>% mutate(Study = factor(Study))
  d_fix   <- long     %>% filter(FixDur > 0)           %>% mutate(Study = factor(Study))
  d_box   <- box_grid %>% mutate(Study = factor(Study))

  fit_first <- glmmTMB(
    FirstFixBest ~ Difficulty10 * WN * Study + (1 + Difficulty10 || Subject),
    data = d_trial, family = binomial
  )

  fit_dur <- lmer(
    log(FixDur) ~ fix_type * fix_value10 * WN * Study + (1 | Subject),
    data = d_fix
  )

  fit_share <- lmer(
    share ~ type * value10 * WN * Study + (1 | Subject),
    data = d_box
  )

  # One panel per model. Value effects on the share are a few thousandths, so
  # that panel gets four decimals.
  tab <- list(
    "Panel A: First Fixation to Best" = freq_columns(fit_first, "Frequentist (glmmTMB)"),
    "Panel B: log Fixation Duration"  = freq_columns(fit_dur,   "Frequentist (lme4)"),
    "Panel C: Share of Fixations"     = freq_columns(fit_share, "Frequentist (lme4)", digits = 4)
  )
  note <- sd_note(list("Panel A" = sds_freq(fit_first), "Panel B" = sds_freq(fit_dur),
                       "Panel C" = sds_freq(fit_share)))
  save_tex(tab, "fixation_properties", note)
}
```

# Option-Level Attention

The standard option-level attentional biases, as a benchmark for the
attribute-level results.

## Net fixation bias

Corrected choice is the actual choice minus the probability of choosing left
predicted from value alone, so it is zero on average and any dependence on
dwell time is attention doing work beyond value. The value-only model is one
plain logistic regression per study.

```{r corrected-choice}
pas$CorrChoice <- NA_real_
for (s in 1:2) {
  rows <- pas$Study == s
  value_only <- glm(ChooseL ~ Diff, data = pas[rows, ], family = binomial)
  pas$CorrChoice[rows] <- pas$ChooseL[rows] -
    predict(value_only, newdata = pas[rows, ], type = "response")
}

# Bin net dwell time (left minus right, seconds) into 0.5 s bins, pooling the
# tails beyond +/- 3 s. Each bin is plotted at its mean net dwell time.
bin_breaks <- c(-Inf, seq(-3, 3, by = 0.5), Inf)
pas <- pas %>% mutate(DwellDiff_bin = cut(DwellDiff, breaks = bin_breaks))

pdata_netfix <- pas %>%
  filter(!is.na(DwellDiff_bin)) %>%
  group_by(Study, Subject, WN, DwellDiff_bin) %>%
  summarise(y_subject = mean(CorrChoice), x_subject = mean(DwellDiff), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Study, WN, DwellDiff_bin) %>%
  summarise(
    x  = mean(x_subject),
    y  = mean(y_subject),
    se = sd(y_subject) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# One plot per study. Only net dwell times between -2 and 2 s are shown: beyond
# that the bins are sparse and just add noise. coord_cartesian() crops the view
# without dropping the data, so the lines still run out to the edge of the plot.
# The x-axis ends exactly at -2 and 2 (no padding); y keeps its usual padding.
# This row has no legend of its own: its line-style key differs from the fitted
# curves below, so patchwork couldn't merge the two. The Range legend comes
# from the last-fixation row.
p_netfix <- list()
for (s in 1:2) {
  p_netfix[[s]] <- ggplot(pdata_netfix %>% filter(Study == s),
                          aes(x = x, y = y, color = WN, shape = WN)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50") +
    geom_line(linewidth = .linewidth) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se), size = pt_size, linewidth = .linewidth) +
    wn_scales +
    labs(x = "Net Dwell Time to Left (s)", y = "Corrected Pr(Choose Left)", title = paste("Study", s)) +
    .myPlot + strip_style + study_title + legend_right +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1.25, 1.25), expand = c(top = TRUE, right = FALSE, bottom = TRUE, left = FALSE)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.2, 0.2, by = 0.1), labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) 
}
```

## Last fixation bias

Probability of choosing the option that was fixated last, as a function of how
much better that option was than the other one, split by the attribute type of
the box that was fixated last.

```{r last-fixation}
pdata_last <- pas %>%
  filter(!is.na(LastSide)) %>%
  mutate(LastType = factor(LastType, levels = c("N", "B", "P"))) %>%
  group_by(Study, Subject, WN, LastType, RelDiff_last) %>%
  summarise(y_subject = mean(ChooseLast), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Study, WN, LastType, RelDiff_last) %>%
  summarise(y = mean(y_subject), se = sd(y_subject) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop")

# Facets are the attribute type of the box that was fixated last.
p_last <- list()
for (s in 1:2) {
  p_last[[s]] <- ggplot(pdata_last %>% filter(Study == s),
                        aes(x = RelDiff_last, y = y, color = WN, shape = WN)) +
    facet_wrap(~ LastType, labeller = type_labels) +

    geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50") +
    geom_line(linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se), size = pt_size, linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
    #stat_smooth(method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "binomial"), se = FALSE, linewidth = .linewidth) +
    wn_scales +
    labs(x = "Value Difference (Last Fixated - Other)", y = "Pr(Choose Last Fixated)") +
    .myPlot + type_strip_style + legend_right
}
```

Both pooled across studies, with study crossed with every other predictor
(Study 1 and Narrow are the reference levels). Net fixation bias: choice on
value difference, net dwell time, and range, with subject random slopes on
value. Last fixation bias: choosing the last-fixated option on its relative
value, the type of the last-fixated box, and range.

```{r option-regressions}
if (RUN_REGRESSIONS) {
  d <- pas %>% mutate(Study = factor(Study))

  fit_netfix <- glmmTMB(
    ChooseL ~ Diff10 * DwellDiff * WN * Study + (1 + Diff10 | Subject),

    data = d %>% filter(!is.na(LastSide)), family = binomial
  )

  # One panel per model.
  tab <- list(
    "Panel A: Choose Left"         = freq_columns(fit_netfix, "Frequentist (glmmTMB)"),
    "Panel B: Choose Last Fixated" = freq_columns(fit_last,   "Frequentist (glmmTMB)")
  )
```

```{r text-lastfix-bias}
if (RUN_REGRESSIONS) {
  # Log-odds of choosing the last-fixated option at equal value, for every
  # type x range cell and study (P, Narrow and Study 1 are the reference
  # levels; other cells add the matching main effects and interactions).
  cells <- tibble()
  for (s in 1:2) {
    for (rng in c("Narrow", "Wide")) {
      for (tt in c("P", "N", "B")) {
        terms <- c("(Intercept)",
                   if (tt != "P") paste0("LastType", tt),
                   if (rng == "Wide") "WNWide",
                   if (tt != "P" && rng == "Wide") paste0("LastType", tt, ":WNWide"),
                   if (s == 2) "Study2",
                   if (s == 2 && tt != "P") paste0("LastType", tt, ":Study2"),
                   if (s == 2 && rng == "Wide") "WNWide:Study2",
                   if (s == 2 && tt != "P" && rng == "Wide") paste0("LastType", tt, ":WNWide:Study2"))
        ci <- coef_ci(fit_last, terms)
        cells <- bind_rows(cells, tibble(Study = s, type = tt, WN = rng,
                                         estimate = ci[["estimate"]], lo = ci[["lo"]], hi = ci[["hi"]]))
      }
    }
  }
  cells

  # Report the smallest and largest cell of each study.
  out <- c()
  for (s in 1:2) {

    for (r in list(d[which.min(d$estimate), ], d[which.max(d$estimate), ])) {
      out <- c(out, paste0("$\\beta^{\\text{Last, ", r$type, ", ", r$WN, "}}_{\\text{Study ", s, "}} = ", fmt_ci(r$estimate, r$lo, r$hi), "$"))
    }
  }
  save_text(paste(out, collapse = ", "), "lastfix_bias")
}
```

# Attribute-Level Attention

The central analysis. A **signed attention weight** is the effect of one second
of dwell on a box on the log-odds of choosing that box's option, holding the
values of all four boxes constant. One weight per (type x value) cell, with
partial pooling: every subject gets their own weight per cell, and we report
the population weight. Positive means attention pulls choice toward the
attended option; negative means it pushes choice away.

Value is held constant without assuming a linear value function: every
(type x value) cell also gets a **utility**, the log-odds contribution of
having that value on an option. Its regressor is the cell's signed presence
(+1 if the cell's box is on the left, -1 on the right, 0 if not on screen).
Each attribute type has one box on each side of a trial, so a type's six
presence columns sum to zero on every trial and only differences between the
utilities of a type are identified: the lowest value of each type is the
reference (utility 0) and the other five are relative to it. A dwell weight is
then estimated only from how dwell on a box varies across the trials on which
that box is shown. With a linear value function instead (the model in the
first version of this notebook, now under Extra Analyses), any gap between a
value's true utility and the line landed on that cell's dwell weight, because
dwell on a shown box is always positive.

Narrow and Wide have partly different value sets, so there is one model per
range condition. Each model pools both studies: the design (value sets,
constraints, instructions) was identical, and fits with separate weights per
study agree (Extra Analyses). A Study 2 term on the intercept lets the side
bias differ between studies.

These are the only Bayesian models in the notebook. With a random slope per
subject for every one of the 18 cells, maximum likelihood (glmmTMB) did not
converge and pushed several cell variances to zero; the weakly informative
priors and partial pooling in brms keep the cell weights well behaved.

The figure puts the data's weights (left) next to the weights that the main
Bayesian model produces out of sample (right). The model itself is fit in
`notebooks/bayesian_model.Rmd` and `code/fitting/`; here we only load its
held-out choice probabilities.

## Design matrices

Per trial: choice, a Study 2 indicator, the signed presence of every
(type x value) cell except the three references (`U_*`), and the signed dwell
time in every cell.

```{r flex-design}
# `bl` (box level) and `ps` (trial level) are the real data by default. The
# Bayesian model section passes simulated trials instead.
build_flex_dat <- function(range, bl = boxlong, ps = pas) {
  bl <- bl %>% filter(WN == range)
  ps <- ps %>% filter(WN == range)

  # Signed dwell per cell. One column per cell, 0 where that cell wasn't on screen.
  dwell_design <- bl %>%
    group_by(Subject, Trial, cell) %>%
    summarise(sd = sum(signed_dwell), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = cell, values_from = sd, values_fill = 0)

  # Signed presence per cell: +1 if the cell's box is on the left, -1 if on the
  # right, 0 if not on screen. Its coefficient is the utility of that value.
  # A type's six columns sum to zero on every trial (one box per side), so the
  # lowest value of each type is dropped: it is the reference with utility 0.
  util_design <- bl %>%
    group_by(Subject, Trial, cell) %>%
    summarise(sp = sum(side_sign), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = cell, values_from = sp, values_fill = 0, names_prefix = "U_")
  ref_cells <- bl %>%
    distinct(type, value, cell) %>%
    group_by(type) %>%
    slice_min(value, n = 1) %>%
    pull(cell)
  util_design <- util_design %>% select(-all_of(paste0("U_", ref_cells)))

  # S2 is the Study 2 indicator for the intercept. (It is not called "Study2"
  # because the table helpers treat a term named Study2 as an interaction.)
  ps %>%
    transmute(Subject, Trial, ChooseL, S2 = as.integer(Study == 2), Study = factor(Study)) %>%
    left_join(util_design,  by = c("Subject", "Trial")) %>%
    left_join(dwell_design, by = c("Subject", "Trial"))
}

# Names of the utility and dwell regressors in a design.
util_cols  <- function(dat) str_subset(names(dat), "^U_")
dwell_cols <- function(dat) str_subset(names(dat), "^[PNB]_(neg|pos)[0-9]+$")

# Population utility for every value and population weight for every cell,
# pooled over studies, plus subject-level random slopes on every utility
# (uncorrelated) and on every cell weight (correlated).
build_flex_formula <- function(dat) {
  as.formula(paste(
    "ChooseL ~ 1 + S2 +", paste(util_cols(dat), collapse = " + "), "+", paste(dwell_cols(dat), collapse = " + "),
    "+ (0 +", paste(util_cols(dat),  collapse = " + "), "|| Subject)",
    "+ (0 +", paste(dwell_cols(dat), collapse = " + "), "| Subject)"
  ))
}
```

## Fits

Sampling each of these takes many hours. `code/fitting/sample_pooled_attention_weights.R`
runs exactly this chunk from a terminal (so a closed R session can't kill it),
optionally for one range at a time, and leaves the caches in
`notebooks/brm_fits/`; after that the notebook only loads them.

```{r flex-fit-by-range}
range_files <- c(
  Narrow = "attention_weights_utility_narrow",
  Wide   = "attention_weights_utility_wide"
)

# The terminal script can set fit_ranges to a single range before running this chunk.
if (!exists("fit_ranges")) fit_ranges <- c("Narrow", "Wide")

flex_fit_range <- list()
for (rng in fit_ranges) {
  flex_dat <- build_flex_dat(rng)
  flex_fit_range[[rng]] <- load_or_fit(
    range_files[[rng]],
    formula = build_flex_formula(flex_dat),
    data    = flex_dat,
    family  = bernoulli(),
    prior   = brms_priors,
    chains  = BRMS_CHAINS, iter = 4000, seed = BRMS_SEED,
    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12)
  )
}
```

## Figures

```{r flex-summary}
# Pull the population-level draws out of each fit once (the fits are big, so
# we don't want to go back to them for every cell).
flex_draws <- list()
for (rng in names(flex_fit_range)) {
  if (!is.null(flex_fit_range[[rng]])) {
    flex_draws[[rng]] <- as_draws_df(flex_fit_range[[rng]], variable = "^b_", regex = TRUE)
  }
}

# Draws of one cell's attention weight, e.g. aw_draws("Narrow", "N_neg30"), and
# of one cell's utility, e.g. u_draws("Narrow", "P_pos10"). The fits pool the
# studies, so there is one population value per cell.
aw_draws <- function(range, cell) flex_draws[[range]][[paste0("b_", cell)]]
u_draws  <- function(range, cell) flex_draws[[range]][[paste0("b_U_", cell)]]

# Parse cell names such as "N_neg30" into a type and a value for plotting.
parse_cells <- function(df) {
  df %>% mutate(
    type  = factor(str_sub(cell, 1, 1), levels = c("N", "B", "P")),
    value = as.numeric(str_extract(cell, "[0-9]+$")) * if_else(str_detect(cell, "_neg"), -1, 1)
  )
}

# Median and 95% HDI of every cell's attention weight in one range condition.
summarise_flex_weights <- function(range) {
  cells <- names(flex_draws[[range]]) %>% str_subset("^b_[PNB]_(neg|pos)[0-9]+$") %>% str_remove("^b_")
  out <- tibble()
  for (cell in cells) {
    x <- aw_draws(range, cell)
    h <- bayestestR::hdi(x, ci = 0.95)
    out <- bind_rows(out, tibble(WN = range, cell = cell, estimate = median(x), lo = h$CI_low, hi = h$CI_high))
  }
  parse_cells(out)
}

# The same for the utilities. The reference of each type (its lowest value in
# this range) is put back at 0 so that the whole value function can be drawn.
summarise_flex_utilities <- function(range) {
  cells <- names(flex_draws[[range]]) %>% str_subset("^b_U_") %>% str_remove("^b_U_")
  out <- tibble()
  for (cell in cells) {
    x <- u_draws(range, cell)
    h <- bayestestR::hdi(x, ci = 0.95)
    out <- bind_rows(out, tibble(WN = range, cell = cell, estimate = median(x), lo = h$CI_low, hi = h$CI_high))
  }
  refs <- boxlong %>%
    filter(WN == range) %>%
    distinct(type, value, cell) %>%
    group_by(type) %>%
    slice_min(value, n = 1) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    transmute(WN = range, cell, estimate = 0, lo = 0, hi = 0)
  parse_cells(bind_rows(out, refs))
}

# One quantity (attention weight or utility) by type and value, Narrow and
# Wide overlaid.
plot_by_range <- function(d, title, ylab, ylim = NULL) {
  ggplot(d, aes(x = value, y = estimate, color = WN, shape = WN)) +
    facet_wrap(~ type, scales = "free_x", labeller = type_labels) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50") +
    geom_line(linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), size = pt_size, linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
    wn_scales +
    labs(x = "Attribute Value", y = ylab, title = title) +
    .myPlot + type_strip_style + study_title + legend_right + theme(legend.direction = "vertical") +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = x_attr_breaks)
}

# Data (points with their intervals, no connecting lines) and a model (lines,
# no points) in the same panels, Narrow and Wide overlaid: geometry tells data
# from model, color tells the range condition. The model's simulation error is
# not drawn; it shrinks with the number of simulated choices.
plot_overlay <- function(data_w, model_w, title, ylab, ylim = NULL) {
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = value, color = WN)) +
    facet_wrap(~ type, scales = "free_x", labeller = type_labels) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50") +
    geom_line(data = model_w, aes(y = estimate, group = WN), linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
    geom_pointrange(data = data_w, aes(y = estimate, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, shape = WN),
                    size = pt_size, linewidth = .linewidth, position = wn_dodge) +
    wn_scales +
    labs(x = "Attribute Value", y = ylab, title = title) +
    .myPlot + type_strip_style + study_title + legend_right + theme(legend.direction = "vertical") +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = x_attr_breaks)
}
```

### Bayesian model

The main Bayesian model: one prior per range condition, with loss aversion.
Every trial's choice probability is held out (12-fold cross-validation, blocks
of five trial positions per subject, every fold fit from scratch), so the
model never saw the trial it predicts. Ten replicates of one choice per
trial are drawn from those probabilities, and each replicate is run through
the same regression as the data, with the same brms model, priors and
sampler, as its own dataset (so the hierarchical model sees the data's
design), on Compute Canada (`code/fitting/compute_canada_attention_weights.R`;
`bayesian_model.Rmd` does the same for every model variant). Only a compact
summary of each fit comes back,
`notebooks/brm_fits/attention_weights_utility_sim_cond_lam_<range>_rep<k>_draws.rds`.
The chunk pools the replicates by stacking their draws (the average of their
posteriors) and takes the median and 95% HDI of every cell weight; the
overlay draws only the medians.

```{r bayes-weights}
# The held-out predictions of the main model; the Extra Analyses section
# reads them for the participants' log-likelihoods.
bayes_loo_file <- file.path(bayes_dir, "loo_cond_lam.rds")

# The cluster fits of the main model's simulated choices: one file per
# replicate and range condition, holding the population-level draws of the
# same brms model as the data's. The replicates' draws are stacked (the
# average of their posteriors); posterior median and 95% HDI of every cell
# weight, parsed into type and value.
weights_model <- tibble()
for (rng in c("Narrow", "Wide")) {
  files <- list.files(fit_dir, full.names = TRUE,
                      pattern = paste0("^attention_weights_utility_sim_cond_lam_", tolower(rng), "_rep[0-9]+_draws\\.rds$"))
  if (length(files) == 0) { cat("No cluster fit for cond_lam", rng, "in", fit_dir, "\n"); next }
  cat(rng, ": ", length(files), " replicate(s)\n", sep = "")
  draws <- bind_rows(lapply(files, function(f) as_tibble(readRDS(f)$draws) %>% select(matches("^b_"))))
  for (cell in names(draws) %>% str_subset("^b_[PNB]_(neg|pos)[0-9]+$") %>% str_remove("^b_")) {
    x <- draws[[paste0("b_", cell)]]
    h <- bayestestR::hdi(x, ci = 0.95)
    weights_model <- bind_rows(weights_model, tibble(WN = rng, cell = cell, estimate = median(x), lo = h$CI_low, hi = h$CI_high))
  }
}
if (nrow(weights_model) > 0) {
  weights_model <- weights_model %>% mutate(WN = factor(WN, levels = c("Narrow", "Wide"))) %>% parse_cells()
}

# The right panel of the figure.
p_weights_model <- NULL
if (nrow(weights_model) > 0) {
  p_weights_model <- plot_by_range(weights_model, "Bayesian Model", "Attention Weight", c(-0.5, 0.5))
}
```

## Tables

Population-level coefficients of the two brms fits (posterior median and 95%
HDI) in one table: Narrow and Wide are the columns, the utilities (with the
intercept and the Study 2 term) are Panel A and the attention weights Panel B.
Rows are aligned by cell, so a value that only one range shows is blank in the
other column. Panel A also prints each type's reference, its lowest value, as
"0 (reference)". The Bayesian R2 takes a minute or two per fit.

```{r flex-tables}
if (RUN_REGRESSIONS && length(flex_draws) == 2) {
  panel_a <- list()
  panel_b <- list()
  sds     <- list()
  for (rng in c("Narrow", "Wide")) {
    fit   <- flex_fit_range[[rng]]
    coefs <- order_cells(tidy_brms(fit))
    is_w  <- str_detect(coefs$term, "^[PNB]_(neg|pos)[0-9]+$")   # the attention weights
    # Panel A also lists each type's reference: its lowest value, whose utility
    # is fixed at zero by construction and so has no coefficient in the fit. It
    # is the one cell of the type that has a weight but no utility.
    cells   <- coefs$term[is_w]
    ref     <- cells[!paste0("U_", cells) %in% coefs$term]
    stopifnot(length(ref) == 3)   # one per type
    ref_row <- tibble(term = paste0("U_", ref), estimate = 0, conf.low = NA_real_, conf.high = NA_real_,
                      text = "0 (reference)")
    utilities <- order_cells(bind_rows(coefs[!is_w, ], ref_row))
    # The fit statistics go under Panel B, at the bottom of the table.
    panel_a[[rng]] <- table_columns(utilities, tibble(), c("ref" = rng))[[1]]
    panel_b[[rng]] <- table_columns(coefs[is_w, ],  gof_brms(fit), c("ref" = rng))[[1]]
    s <- sds_brms(fit)
    sds[[paste0(rng, ", utilities")]] <- s[str_detect(names(s), "^U_")]
    sds[[paste0(rng, ", weights")]]   <- s[!str_detect(names(s), "^U_")]
  }
  tab <- list(
    "Panel A: Utility of each value, relative to the lowest value of its type" = panel_a,
    "Panel B: Attention weight per second of dwell"                            = panel_b
  )
  # Rows in type and value order over the union of both ranges' cells (left to
  # itself, modelsummary would put the Wide-only values at the bottom).
  all_cells <- unique(unlist(lapply(flex_draws, function(d) {
    names(d) %>% str_subset("^b_[PNB]_(neg|pos)[0-9]+$") %>% str_remove("^b_")
  })))
  row_order <- c("Intercept", "Study 2", label_term(all_cells[cell_order(all_cells)]))
  save_tex(tab, "attribute_level_attention",
           sd_note(sds, intro = paste("A blank cell is a value that does not occur in that range condition.",
                                      "Random-effect SDs across subjects (posterior medians).")),
           ci_inline = TRUE, coef_order = row_order)
}
```

## Text Output

The attention weights quoted in the Attribute-Level Attention paragraphs of
the paper. Each snippet reports one attribute value per range condition as
`fmt_post(aw_draws(range, cell))`, written
`$\omega^{\text{Narrow}, -30} = -0.132\ [-0.219, -0.055]$`.

```{r text-attn-helpers}
# One attention weight in the paper's notation: range condition in the
# superscript, attribute type in the subscript, the value in parentheses, e.g.
# omega_label("\\text{Narrow}", "N_neg30") -> \omega^{\text{Narrow}}_{\text{N}}(-30).
omega_label <- function(sup, cell) {
  v <- str_extract(cell, "[0-9]+$")
  if (str_detect(cell, "_neg")) v <- paste0("-", v)
  paste0("\\omega^{", sup, "}_{\\text{", str_sub(cell, 1, 1), "}}(", v, ")")
}

# One snippet from the cells of each range, e.g.
# list(Narrow = c("N_neg30", "N_neg25"), Wide = c("N_neg50", "N_neg40")) ->
# "$\omega^{\text{Narrow}}_{\text{N}}(-30) = -0.211\ [-0.287, -0.134]$, ...",
# the Narrow cells first, each range's cells in the order given. A named
# vector with one cell per range works too.
omega_text <- function(cells, digits = 3) {
  out <- c()
  for (rng in names(cells)) {
    for (cell in cells[[rng]]) {
      out <- c(out, paste0("$", omega_label(paste0("\\text{", rng, "}"), cell), " = ",
                           fmt_post(aw_draws(rng, cell), digits), "$"))
    }
  }
  paste(out, collapse = ", ")
}

# The Narrow minus Wide difference of one cell's weight: the two fits are
# independent, so the difference of draws is the posterior of the difference.
omega_diff_text <- function(cell, digits = 3) {
  paste0("$", omega_label("\\text{Narrow} - \\text{Wide}", cell), " = ",
         fmt_post(aw_draws("Narrow", cell) - aw_draws("Wide", cell), digits), "$")
}

# The difference between two attribute types at the values they share, e.g.
# omega_type_diff_text("B", "P") -> "$\omega^{\text{Narrow}}_{\text{B} - \text{P}}(5) = ...$, ...":
# type a minus type b, at every value both types take in a range (from the
# design), Narrow first. Both weights come from the same range's fit, so the
# difference of draws is the posterior of the difference.
cell_name <- function(type, value) paste0(type, "_", if_else(value < 0, "neg", "pos"), abs(value))
omega_type_diff_text <- function(a, b, digits = 3) {
  out <- c()
  for (rng in c("Narrow", "Wide")) {
    vals <- boxlong %>% filter(WN == rng) %>% distinct(type, value)
    shared <- sort(intersect(vals$value[vals$type == a], vals$value[vals$type == b]))
    for (v in shared) {
      d <- aw_draws(rng, cell_name(a, v)) - aw_draws(rng, cell_name(b, v))
      out <- c(out, paste0("$\\omega^{\\text{", rng, "}}_{\\text{", a, "} - \\text{", b, "}}(", v, ") = ",
                           fmt_post(d, digits), "$"))
    }
  }
  paste(out, collapse = ", ")
}
write_attn <- RUN_REGRESSIONS && length(flex_draws) == 2
```

```{r text-attn-aversive}
if (write_attn) {
  # The two lowest aversive values of each range: -30, -25 (Narrow); -50, -40 (Wide).
  save_text(omega_text(list(Narrow = c("N_neg30", "N_neg25"), Wide = c("N_neg50", "N_neg40"))), "attn_N_lowest")
  # The two middle values: -20, -15 (Narrow); -30, -20 (Wide).
  save_text(omega_text(list(Narrow = c("N_neg20", "N_neg15"), Wide = c("N_neg30", "N_neg20"))), "attn_N_middle")
  # The two highest (still negative) values, -10 and -5 in both ranges.
  save_text(omega_text(list(Narrow = c("N_neg10", "N_neg5"), Wide = c("N_neg10", "N_neg5"))), "attn_N_highest")
  # The maximum aversive value on its own, -5 in both ranges.
  save_text(omega_text(c(Narrow = "N_neg5", Wide = "N_neg5")), "attn_N_max")
  # The one middle value whose interval does not include 0: -40 in Wide.
  save_text(omega_text(c(Wide = "N_neg40")), "attn_N_neg40_wide")
  # -30 is the lowest value in Narrow but a middle value in Wide: each range's
  # weight, and the Narrow minus Wide difference.
  save_text(omega_text(c(Narrow = "N_neg30")), "attn_N_neg30_narrow")
  save_text(omega_text(c(Wide = "N_neg30")), "attn_N_neg30_wide")
  save_text(omega_diff_text("N_neg30"), "attn_N_neg30_diff")
}
```

# Range Sensitivity

A value-representation test rather than an attention test: does a given value
difference move choice more in the Narrow range than in the Wide range? Choice
is regressed on the three per-type value channels, each crossed with range and
study, with subject-level random intercepts and slopes on the three channels.
Range normalization predicts steeper slopes in Narrow. This model has only four
random effects per subject, so like the other small models it is fit by
maximum likelihood (glmmTMB) rather than brms.

```{r value-fit}
# Signed value per type (value only, no dwell time), for every trial.
value_design <- boxlong %>%
  group_by(Subject, Trial, type) %>%
  summarise(SV = sum(signed_value), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = SV, names_prefix = "SV_", values_fill = 0)

val_dat <- pas %>%
  transmute(Study = factor(Study), Subject, Trial, ChooseL, WN) %>%
  left_join(value_design, by = c("Subject", "Trial"))

fit_val <- glmmTMB(
  ChooseL ~ (SV_P + SV_N + SV_B) * WN * Study + (1 + SV_P + SV_N + SV_B | Subject),
  data = val_dat, family = binomial
)
```

```{r value-readout}
# Narrow and Study 1 are the reference levels, so each (type, range, study)
# slope is a sum of coefficients:
#   Narrow, Study 1: b_SV
#   Wide,   Study 1: b_SV + b_SV:WNWide
#   Narrow, Study 2: b_SV + b_SV:Study2
#   Wide,   Study 2: b_SV + b_SV:WNWide + b_SV:Study2 + b_SV:WNWide:Study2
# "Wide - Narrow" is the Wide terms that are not in the Narrow sum.
slopes <- tibble()
for (s in 1:2) {
  for (tt in c("N", "B", "P")) {
    sv <- paste0("SV_", tt)
    narrow_terms <- c(sv, if (s == 2) paste0(sv, ":Study2"))
    wide_terms   <- c(narrow_terms, paste0(sv, ":WNWide"), if (s == 2) paste0(sv, ":WNWide:Study2"))
    for (q in c("Narrow", "Wide", "Wide - Narrow")) {
      terms <- switch(q, "Narrow" = narrow_terms, "Wide" = wide_terms,
                      "Wide - Narrow" = setdiff(wide_terms, narrow_terms))
      ci <- coef_ci(fit_val, terms)
      slopes <- bind_rows(slopes, tibble(
        Study = paste0("Study ", s), type = tt, quantity = q,
        estimate = ci[["estimate"]], lo = ci[["lo"]], hi = ci[["hi"]]
      ))
    }
  }
}
slopes <- slopes %>% mutate(type = factor(type, levels = c("N", "B", "P")))

slopes %>% mutate(across(c(estimate, lo, hi), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

```{r fig-range-sensitivity, fig.width=2 * .figw, fig.height=1 * .figh}
pdata_val <- slopes %>%
  filter(quantity %in% c("Narrow", "Wide")) %>%
  mutate(WN = factor(quantity, levels = c("Narrow", "Wide")),
         Study = str_remove(Study, "Study "))

p_val <- ggplot(pdata_val, aes(x = type, y = estimate, color = WN, shape = WN)) +
  facet_wrap(~ Study, labeller = study_labels) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), size = 0.8, linewidth = .linewidth,
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  wn_scales +
  labs(x = "Attribute Type", y = "Range Sensitivity (Slope)") + #(log-odds per 10 points)
  .myPlot + strip_style + legend_right + theme(legend.direction = "vertical")

# 1 row x 2 columns (Study 1, Study 2).
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "range_sensitivity.pdf"), p_val, width = 2 * .figw, height = 1 * .figh)
p_val
```

```{r value-table}
}
```
