# Extra Analyses

Analyses that are not in the paper, kept in case we want them again. Nothing
in this section runs unless the switch below is TRUE.

```{r extra-switch}
run_extra_analyses <- FALSE
```

## Attention weights with linear value channels, by study (pre-registered)

The pre-registered attention-weight model, which the paper used as its main
model before the per-value utilities (see the Attribute-Level Attention
section): the three signed values enter as linear channels (`SV_P`, `SV_N`,
`SV_B`) instead of one utility per value, and every coefficient is crossed
with study (Study 1 is the reference level, so a Study 2 weight is the Study 1
weight plus the cell's `:Study2` interaction). Because it was pre-registered
it is reported in the last supplementary section of the paper, so this
subsection writes its figure (`paper/figures/attribute_level_attention_preregistered.pdf`)
and its two tables (`paper/tables/attribute_level_attention_weights_preregistered_narrow.tex`
and `_wide.tex`) when the switch above is on.

It also does two jobs for the main text. Its by-study weights are the
evidence that the two studies agree, which justifies pooling them in the main
model: they correlate at 0.81 across the 36 cells, and 4 of the 36
cell-by-study interactions exclude zero, about what chance gives at 95%. And
it shows what the linear channel does to a cell weight: dwell on a shown box
is always positive, so any gap between a value's utility and the line lands on
that cell's dwell weight. That is why the P, 5 weight in Narrow is clearly
positive here and not in the main model. The cached fits are the ones sampled
in October 2026.

```{r extra-linear-fit}
if (run_extra_analyses) {
  # Like build_flex_dat(), with the three signed value channels in place of
  # the utility columns.
  build_flex_dat_linear <- function(range, bl = boxlong, ps = pas) {
    bl <- bl %>% filter(WN == range)
    ps <- ps %>% filter(WN == range)
    dwell_design <- bl %>%
      group_by(Subject, Trial, cell) %>%
      summarise(sd = sum(signed_dwell), .groups = "drop") %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = cell, values_from = sd, values_fill = 0)
    # Signed value per attribute type. These three sum to Diff / 10.
    value_design <- bl %>%
      group_by(Subject, Trial, type) %>%
      summarise(SV = sum(signed_value), .groups = "drop") %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = SV, names_prefix = "SV_", values_fill = 0)
    ps %>%
      transmute(Subject, Trial, ChooseL, Study = factor(Study)) %>%
      left_join(value_design, by = c("Subject", "Trial")) %>%
      left_join(dwell_design, by = c("Subject", "Trial"))
  }

  # Every value channel and cell weight crossed with study, plus subject-level
  # random slopes on the value channels and on every cell.
  build_flex_formula_linear <- function(dat) {
    value_cols <- c("SV_P", "SV_N", "SV_B")
    as.formula(paste(
      "ChooseL ~ (", paste(c(value_cols, dwell_cols(dat)), collapse = " + "), ") * Study",
      "+ (0 + SV_P + SV_N + SV_B | Subject)",
      "+ (0 +", paste(dwell_cols(dat), collapse = " + "), "| Subject)"
    ))
  }

  linear_files <- c(
    Narrow = "flex_attention_weights_pooled_narrow",
    Wide   = "flex_attention_weights_pooled_wide"
  )
  linear_fit <- list()
  for (rng in c("Narrow", "Wide")) {
    linear_dat <- build_flex_dat_linear(rng)
    linear_fit[[rng]] <- load_or_fit(
      linear_files[[rng]],
      formula = build_flex_formula_linear(linear_dat),
      data    = linear_dat,
      family  = bernoulli(),
      prior   = brms_priors,
      chains  = BRMS_CHAINS, iter = 4000, seed = BRMS_SEED,
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12)
    )
  }
}
```

```{r extra-linear-plots, fig.width=2 * .figw, fig.height=1 * .figh}
if (run_extra_analyses) {
  linear_draws <- list()
  for (rng in names(linear_fit)) {
    if (!is.null(linear_fit[[rng]])) {
      linear_draws[[rng]] <- as_draws_df(linear_fit[[rng]], variable = "^b_", regex = TRUE)
    }

  # Draws of one cell weight for one study, e.g. aw_draws_linear("Narrow", "N_neg30", 2).
  aw_draws_linear <- function(range, cell, study) {
    d <- linear_draws[[range]]
    if (study == 1) d[[paste0("b_", cell)]] else d[[paste0("b_", cell)]] + d[[paste0("b_", cell, ":Study2")]]
  }

  # Median and 95% HDI of every cell weight, by range and study.
  weights_linear <- tibble()
  for (rng in names(linear_draws)) {
    cells <- names(linear_draws[[rng]]) %>% str_subset("^b_[PNB]_(neg|pos)[0-9]+$") %>% str_remove("^b_")
    for (s in 1:2) {
      for (cell in cells) {
        x <- aw_draws_linear(rng, cell, s)
        h <- bayestestR::hdi(x, ci = 0.95)
        weights_linear <- bind_rows(weights_linear, tibble(
          Study = s, WN = rng, cell = cell, estimate = median(x), lo = h$CI_low, hi = h$CI_high
        ))
      }
    }
  }

  # One panel per study, Narrow and Wide overlaid. Saved for the supplement.
  p_linear <- list()
  if (nrow(weights_linear) > 0) {
    weights_linear <- parse_cells(weights_linear) %>% mutate(WN = factor(WN, levels = c("Narrow", "Wide")))
    for (s in 1:2) {
      key <- paste0("Study ", s)
      p_linear[[key]] <- plot_by_range(weights_linear %>% filter(Study == s), key, "Attention Weight", c(-0.5, 0.5))
    }
  }
  fig_linear <- (get_or_spacer(p_linear, "Study 1") | get_or_spacer(p_linear, "Study 2")) + plot_layout(guides = "collect")
  if (length(p_linear) == 2) {
    ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "attribute_level_attention_preregistered.pdf"), fig_linear, width = 2 * .figw, height = 1 * .figh)
  }
  fig_linear
}
```

```{r extra-linear-text}
  # How well the two studies agree in the pre-registered model, quoted in the
  # supplement: the correlation between the Study 1 and Study 2 cell weights
  # across all 36 cells (18 per range), and how many of the 36 cell x Study 2
  # interactions have a 95% HDI that excludes 0 (1.8 expected by chance).
  by_study <- weights_linear %>%

            "attn_prereg_agreement")
```

## Attention weights by study (utility model)

Robustness check for pooling the two studies in the main model: the same
per-value-utility model as the Attribute-Level Attention section, with every
population-level coefficient (the intercept, the 15 utilities, and the 18
attention weights) crossed with study. Study 1 is the reference level, so a
Study 2 coefficient is the Study 1 coefficient plus its `:Study2` interaction.
The random slopes are those of the main model (uncorrelated on the utilities,
correlated on the weights). One fit per range condition, sampled from a
terminal with `code/fitting/sample_bystudy_attention_weights.R` (many hours
each). When the switch above is on, this subsection writes the figure
(`paper/figures/attribute_level_attention_by_study.pdf`), the two tables
(`paper/tables/attribute_level_attention_by_study_narrow.tex` and `_wide.tex`)
and the snippets (`attn_bystudy_corr`, `attn_bystudy_siginteractions`, and
`util_bystudy_siginteractions` for the utility interactions) of the paper's
"Attention Weights by Study" supplementary section.

Both fits were sampled on 4-5 November 2026 (7.4 and 6.0 hours). They are
clean on every population-level parameter (no divergences, no treedepth hits,
Rhat at most 1.003, bulk ESS at least 2,500); a few subject-level correlations
in Wide mix more slowly (one Rhat of 1.04 with a bulk ESS of 119), and nothing
below uses them. The Study 1 and Study 2 weights correlate at 0.77 across the
36 cells, and 5 of the 36 weight interactions exclude 0 (1.8 by chance): the
lowest aversive value in Wide (-0.305 in Study 1, -0.072 in Study 2), the two
lowest ambivalent values in Narrow, and the 20 and 30 appetitive values in
Wide. The utilities differ more between the studies: 8 of the 30 utility
interactions exclude 0, all in Wide, where Study 2's utilities rise more
steeply over the lowest aversive values and less steeply over the upper
ambivalent and appetitive values.

```{r extra-bystudy-fit}
if (run_extra_analyses) {
  # The main model's design matrix (build_flex_dat() keeps Study as a factor);
  # the Study 2 intercept term S2 is replaced by the Study interactions.
  build_flex_formula_bystudy <- function(dat) {
    as.formula(paste(
      "ChooseL ~ (1 +", paste(c(util_cols(dat), dwell_cols(dat)), collapse = " + "), ") * Study",
      "+ (0 +", paste(util_cols(dat),  collapse = " + "), "|| Subject)",
      "+ (0 +", paste(dwell_cols(dat), collapse = " + "), "| Subject)"
    ))
  }

  bystudy_files <- c(
    Narrow = "attention_weights_utility_bystudy_narrow",
    Wide   = "attention_weights_utility_bystudy_wide"
  )
  # The terminal script can set bystudy_ranges to a single range before running this chunk.
  if (!exists("bystudy_ranges")) bystudy_ranges <- c("Narrow", "Wide")

  bystudy_fit <- list()
  for (rng in bystudy_ranges) {
    bystudy_dat <- build_flex_dat(rng) %>% select(-S2)
    bystudy_fit[[rng]] <- load_or_fit(
      bystudy_files[[rng]],
      formula = build_flex_formula_bystudy(bystudy_dat),
      data    = bystudy_dat,
      family  = bernoulli(),
      prior   = brms_priors,
      chains  = BRMS_CHAINS, iter = 4000, seed = BRMS_SEED,
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12)
    )
  }
}
```

```{r extra-bystudy-plots, fig.width=2 * .figw, fig.height=1 * .figh}
if (run_extra_analyses) {
  bystudy_draws <- list()
  for (rng in names(bystudy_fit)) {
    if (!is.null(bystudy_fit[[rng]])) {
      bystudy_draws[[rng]] <- as_draws_df(bystudy_fit[[rng]], variable = "^b_", regex = TRUE)
    }
  }

  # Draws of one coefficient for one study: the Study 1 draw, or the Study 1
  # draw plus its Study 2 interaction. `par` is an attention weight such as
  # "N_neg30" or a utility such as "U_N_neg25".
  bystudy_draws_of <- function(range, par, study) {
    d <- bystudy_draws[[range]]
    if (study == 1) d[[paste0("b_", par)]] else d[[paste0("b_", par)]] + d[[paste0("b_", par, ":Study2")]]
  }

  # Median and 95% HDI of every attention weight and every utility, by range
  # and study. As in the main model's figures, each type's reference (lowest)
  # value is put back at 0 for the utilities.
  weights_bystudy   <- tibble()
  utilities_bystudy <- tibble()
  for (rng in names(bystudy_draws)) {
    pars <- names(bystudy_draws[[rng]]) %>% str_subset("^b_(U_)?[PNB]_(neg|pos)[0-9]+$") %>% str_remove("^b_")
    refs <- boxlong %>%
      filter(WN == rng) %>%
      distinct(type, value, cell) %>%
      group_by(type) %>%
      slice_min(value, n = 1) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      pull(cell)
    for (s in 1:2) {
      for (par in pars) {
        x   <- bystudy_draws_of(rng, par, s)
        h   <- bayestestR::hdi(x, ci = 0.95)
        row <- tibble(Study = s, WN = rng, cell = str_remove(par, "^U_"),
                      estimate = median(x), lo = h$CI_low, hi = h$CI_high)
        if (str_detect(par, "^U_")) {
          utilities_bystudy <- bind_rows(utilities_bystudy, row)
        } else {
          weights_bystudy <- bind_rows(weights_bystudy, row)
        }
      }
      utilities_bystudy <- bind_rows(utilities_bystudy,
                                     tibble(Study = s, WN = rng, cell = refs, estimate = 0, lo = 0, hi = 0))
    }
  }

  # One panel per study, Narrow and Wide overlaid: the attention weights (for
  # the supplement) and the utilities (saved for reference).
  p_w <- list()
  p_u <- list()
  if (nrow(weights_bystudy) > 0) {
    weights_bystudy   <- parse_cells(weights_bystudy)   %>% mutate(WN = factor(WN, levels = c("Narrow", "Wide")))
    utilities_bystudy <- parse_cells(utilities_bystudy) %>% mutate(WN = factor(WN, levels = c("Narrow", "Wide")))
    for (s in 1:2) {
      key <- paste0("Study ", s)
      p_w[[key]] <- plot_by_range(weights_bystudy   %>% filter(Study == s), key, "Attention Weight", c(-0.5, 0.5))
      p_u[[key]] <- plot_by_range(utilities_bystudy %>% filter(Study == s), key, "Utility (log-odds)")
    }
  }
  fig_bystudy_weights   <- (get_or_spacer(p_w, "Study 1") | get_or_spacer(p_w, "Study 2")) + plot_layout(guides = "collect")
  fig_bystudy_utilities <- (get_or_spacer(p_u, "Study 1") | get_or_spacer(p_u, "Study 2")) + plot_layout(guides = "collect")
  if (length(p_w) == 2) {
    ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "attribute_level_attention_by_study.pdf"), fig_bystudy_weights,   width = 2 * .figw, height = 1 * .figh)
    ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "attribute_level_utilities_by_study.pdf"), fig_bystudy_utilities, width = 2 * .figw, height = 1 * .figh)
  }
  print(fig_bystudy_weights)
  fig_bystudy_utilities
}
```

```{r extra-bystudy-tables}
if (run_extra_analyses) {
  # One table per range, laid out like the main table (Panel A utilities,
  # Panel B weights) but with the Study 1 coefficient and its Study 2
  # interaction as the columns. These are the files the supplement inputs.
  for (rng in names(bystudy_fit)) {
    fit <- bystudy_fit[[rng]]
    if (is.null(fit)) next
    coefs <- order_cells(tidy_brms(fit))
    is_w  <- str_detect(coefs$term, "^[PNB]_(neg|pos)[0-9]+(:Study2)?$")   # the attention weights
    # Each type's reference (its lowest value) has no utility coefficient in
    # either study: its Study 1 utility and its Study 2 shift are both zero by
    # construction, so Panel A prints "0 (reference)" in both columns.
    cells   <- unique(str_remove(coefs$term[is_w], ":Study2$"))
    ref     <- cells[!paste0("U_", cells) %in% coefs$term]
    stopifnot(length(ref) == 3)   # one per type
    ref_row <- tibble(term = c(paste0("U_", ref), paste0("U_", ref, ":Study2")),
                      estimate = 0, conf.low = NA_real_, conf.high = NA_real_, text = "0 (reference)")
    utilities <- order_cells(bind_rows(coefs[!is_w, ], ref_row))
    # The fit statistics go under Panel B only. table_columns() gives the
    # second column a placeholder Num.Obs. row, which would print as an empty
    # row under Panel A, so Panel A's columns get no fit statistics at all.
    panel_a <- table_columns(utilities, tibble(), study_columns)
    for (k in seq_along(panel_a)) panel_a[[k]]$glance <- tibble()
    tab <- list(
      "Panel A: Utility of each value, relative to the lowest value of its type" = panel_a,
      "Panel B: Attention weight per second of dwell" =
        table_columns(coefs[is_w, ], gof_brms(fit), study_columns)
    )
    s    <- sds_brms(fit)
    note <- sd_note(list("Utilities" = s[str_detect(names(s), "^U_")], "Weights" = s[!str_detect(names(s), "^U_")]),
                    intro = "Random-effect SDs across subjects (posterior medians).")
    save_tex(tab, paste0("attribute_level_attention_by_study_", tolower(rng)), note, ci_inline = TRUE)
  }
}
```

```{r extra-bystudy-text}
if (run_extra_analyses && length(bystudy_draws) == 2) {
  # How well the two studies agree under the utility model, quoted in the
  # supplement: the correlation between the Study 1 and Study 2 attention
  # weights across all 36 cells (18 per range), and the Study 2 interactions
  # (36 on the weights, 30 on the utilities) whose 95% HDI excludes 0, each
  # with its posterior median and HDI (5% of each would by chance).
  by_study <- weights_bystudy %>%
    select(WN, cell, Study, estimate) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Study, values_from = estimate, names_prefix = "S")
  # Pearson correlation of the 36 cell medians, with the p-value of its t-test (34 df).
  ct <- cor.test(by_study$S1, by_study$S2)
  save_text(sprintf("$r = %.2f$, $%s$", ct$estimate, fmt_p(ct$p.value)), "attn_bystudy_corr")

  # A Study 2 interaction in the paper's notation: range condition in the
  # superscript, attribute type and the Study 2 - Study 1 contrast in the
  # subscript, the value in parentheses, e.g.
  # \omega^{\text{Wide}}_{\text{N}, \text{Study 2} - \text{Study 1}}(-50);
  # a utility interaction uses u in place of \omega.
  bystudy_label <- function(rng, par) {
    sym  <- if (str_detect(par, "^U_")) "u" else "\\omega"
    cell <- str_remove(par, "^U_")
    v    <- str_extract(cell, "[0-9]+$")
    if (str_detect(cell, "_neg")) v <- paste0("-", v)
    paste0(sym, "^{\\text{", rng, "}}_{\\text{", str_sub(cell, 1, 1), "}, \\text{Study 2} - \\text{Study 1}}(", v, ")")
  }

  # Narrow first, then Wide; within a range, the cells in type and value order.
  n_excl <- c(weights = 0, utilities = 0)
  n_tot  <- c(weights = 0, utilities = 0)
  sig    <- list(weights = c(), utilities = c())
  for (rng in names(bystudy_draws)) {
    d    <- bystudy_draws[[rng]]
    pars <- names(d) %>% str_subset("^b_(U_)?[PNB]_(neg|pos)[0-9]+:Study2$") %>% str_remove("^b_") %>% str_remove(":Study2$")
    for (par in pars[cell_order(pars)]) {
      x <- d[[paste0("b_", par, ":Study2")]]
      h <- bayestestR::hdi(x, ci = 0.95)
      k <- if (str_detect(par, "^U_")) "utilities" else "weights"
      n_tot[[k]] <- n_tot[[k]] + 1
      if (h$CI_low > 0 || h$CI_high < 0) {
        n_excl[[k]] <- n_excl[[k]] + 1
        sig[[k]]    <- c(sig[[k]], paste0("$", bystudy_label(rng, par), " = ", fmt_post(x), "$"))
      }
    }
  }
  cat(sprintf("%d of %d weight and %d of %d utility interactions exclude 0\n",
              n_excl[["weights"]], n_tot[["weights"]], n_excl[["utilities"]], n_tot[["utilities"]]))
  save_text(paste(sig$weights,   collapse = ", "), "attn_bystudy_siginteractions")
  save_text(paste(sig$utilities, collapse = ", "), "util_bystudy_siginteractions")
}
```

## Attention weights pooled across range conditions

The cell-weight model from the Attribute-Level Attention section, but fit per
study on both range conditions together (so a cell's weight is averaged over
the two ranges it can appear in), without study interactions. These were the
fits used before the by-range models. The cached fits keep the file names from
the original per-study notebooks.

```{r extra-flex-fit}
if (run_extra_analyses) {
  # Like build_flex_dat(), but one study, both ranges, and no Study column.
  build_flex_dat_allranges <- function(study) {
    bl <- boxlong %>% filter(Study == study)
    ps <- pas     %>% filter(Study == study)
    flex_design <- bl %>%
      group_by(Subject, Trial, cell) %>%
      summarise(sd = sum(signed_dwell), .groups = "drop") %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = cell, values_from = sd, values_fill = 0)
    value_design <- bl %>%
      group_by(Subject, Trial, type) %>%
      summarise(SV = sum(signed_value), .groups = "drop") %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = SV, names_prefix = "SV_", values_fill = 0)
    ps %>%
      select(Subject, Trial, ChooseL) %>%
      left_join(value_design, by = c("Subject", "Trial")) %>%
      left_join(flex_design,  by = c("Subject", "Trial"))
  }

  # Like build_flex_formula(), without the study interactions.
  build_flex_formula_allranges <- function(dat) {
    value_cols <- c("SV_P", "SV_N", "SV_B")
    cell_cols  <- setdiff(names(dat), c("Subject", "Trial", "ChooseL", value_cols))
    as.formula(paste(
      "ChooseL ~", paste(value_cols, collapse = " + "), "+",
      paste(cell_cols, collapse = " + "),
      "+ (0 + SV_P + SV_N + SV_B | Subject)",
      "+ (0 +", paste(cell_cols, collapse = " + "), "| Subject)"
    ))
  }

  # The Study 1 fit was sampled with adapt_delta = 0.99, the Study 2 fit with 0.95.
  flex_files <- c(
    "Study 1" = "flex_attention_weights_typeval_partpool",
    "Study 2" = "PAS4_flex_attention_weights_typeval_partpool"
  )
  flex_fit <- list()
  for (s in 1:2) {
    key <- paste0("Study ", s)
    flex_dat <- build_flex_dat_allranges(s)
    flex_fit[[key]] <- load_or_fit(
      flex_files[[key]],
      formula = build_flex_formula_allranges(flex_dat),
      data    = flex_dat,
      family  = bernoulli(),
      prior   = brms_priors,
      chains  = BRMS_CHAINS, iter = 4000, seed = BRMS_SEED,
      control = list(adapt_delta = ifelse(s == 1, 0.99, 0.95), max_treedepth = 12)
    )
  }
}
```

```{r extra-flex-plots, fig.width=2 * .figw, fig.height=1 * .figh}
if (run_extra_analyses) {
  # Cell weights of one fit (no study interactions here, so tidy_brms is enough).
  summarise_flex_weights_allranges <- function(fit) {
    tidy_brms(fit) %>%
      filter(str_detect(term, "^[PNB]_(neg|pos)[0-9]+$")) %>%
      transmute(
        term, estimate, lo = conf.low, hi = conf.high,
        type  = factor(str_sub(term, 1, 1), levels = c("N", "B", "P")),
        value = as.numeric(str_extract(term, "[0-9]+$")) * if_else(str_detect(term, "_neg"), -1, 1)
      )
  }

  # Signed attention weights by type and value (one study). These fits pool the
  # two range conditions, so everything is drawn in black.
  plot_weights <- function(weights, title) {
    ggplot(weights, aes(x = value, y = estimate)) +
      facet_wrap(~ type, scales = "free_x", labeller = type_labels) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey50") +
      geom_line(linewidth = .linewidth) +
      geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), size = pt_size, linewidth = .linewidth, color = "black") +
      labs(x = "Attribute Value", y = "Attention Weight", title = title) +
      .myPlot + type_strip_style + study_title + legend_right + theme(legend.direction = "vertical") +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = x_attr_breaks)
  }

  p_weights <- list()
  for (key in names(flex_fit)) {
    if (!is.null(flex_fit[[key]])) {
      p_weights[[key]] <- plot_weights(summarise_flex_weights_allranges(flex_fit[[key]]), title = key)
    }
  }
  (get_or_spacer(p_weights, "Study 1") | get_or_spacer(p_weights, "Study 2"))
}
```

## Participant-level out-of-sample log-likelihood of the Bayesian model

How large is the out-of-sample log-likelihood that one participant contributes
to the model comparison (the table of estimates in the Bayesian model
supplement)? A participant's total is the sum, over all of their trials, of the
log probability that the main Bayesian model gave to the choice they made,
when it was fit without that trial (the 12-fold cross-validation of
`bayesian_model.Rmd`; `heldout_loglik` clips each probability to
[1e-12, 1 - 1e-12], as in that comparison, and the clip never binds). A
total is a sum over trials, and Study 1 participants have 24 to 30 trials
against 50 to 60 in Study 2, so the mean and SD of the totals are given for
each study. Needs only the cached held-out predictions, so it is quick, but
like the rest of this section it runs only when the switch is TRUE. Snippet:
`bayes_participant_ll`.

```{r extra-participant-ll}
if (run_extra_analyses && file.exists(bayes_loo_file)) {
  # heldout_loglik lives in the Bayesian model's fitting code; load that file
  # into its own environment so that its helper names don't mix with this
  # notebook's.
  fit_code <- new.env()
  source(here::here("code/fitting/fit_bayesian_attributes.R"), local = fit_code)

  # One row per participant: the total log-likelihood over their trials.
  pred    <- readRDS(bayes_loo_file)$pred
  pred$ll <- fit_code$heldout_loglik(pred)
  ll_part <- pred %>%
    group_by(Subject, Study) %>%
    summarise(total = sum(ll), .groups = "drop")

  # Mean and SD of the participants' totals, one pair per study (the study goes
  # in the subscript).
  by_study <- c()
  for (s in 1:2) {
    x <- ll_part$total[ll_part$Study == s]
    by_study <- c(by_study, sprintf("$M_{\\text{Study %d}} = %.2f$, $SD_{\\text{Study %d}} = %.2f$", s, mean(x), s, sd(x)))
  }
  save_text(paste(by_study, collapse = "; "), "bayes_participant_ll")
}
```

## Convergence of the Bayesian regressions

Checks the two sentences in the paper's Methods: every Bayesian model
converged with no divergent transitions, and every group-level parameter
and subject-level random effect had $\hat{R} < 1.01$ and an effective sample
size above 1,000. "Group-level parameters" are the population-level
coefficients (`b_`, the estimates the tables report); the subject-level
random effects are the `r_` terms. Both the bulk and the tail effective
sample size must clear 1,000, and $\hat{R}$ is compared after rounding to two
decimals, as it would be reported, so a value that rounds to 1.01 passes and
one that rounds to 1.02 does not. The random-effect SDs and correlations are not
part of the claim and are not checked (several of them mix more slowly; see
the by-study section above). The models are the six brms fits of the data
whose estimates the paper reports (the main attention-weight model of the
Attribute-Level Attention section, its by-study version and the
pre-registered linear-channel version, one fit per range condition) and the
fits of the main Bayesian model's simulated choices that draw the model lines
of the attribute-level figure; for those only the population-level draws and
the sampler diagnostics were kept (see
`code/fitting/compute_canada_attention_weights.R`), so their subject-level
random effects cannot be checked. The table has one row per fit and level:
the number of parameters, the divergent transitions, the largest $\hat{R}$,
the smallest effective sample size and how many parameters miss either
threshold; the parameters that miss one are listed after it, then the
verdict. Every fit of the data is about 1.4 GB with tens of thousands of
subject-level parameters, so this chunk is slow (about 17 minutes). Snippet:
`brms_convergence`, the largest $\hat{R}$ and the smallest effective sample
size over the checked parameters.

```{r extra-brms-convergence}
if (run_extra_analyses) {
  # The fits of the data that the paper reports, one per range condition.
  paper_fits <- c(
    "Main, Narrow"           = "attention_weights_utility_narrow",
    "Main, Wide"             = "attention_weights_utility_wide",
    "By study, Narrow"       = "attention_weights_utility_bystudy_narrow",
    "By study, Wide"         = "attention_weights_utility_bystudy_wide",
    "Pre-registered, Narrow" = "flex_attention_weights_pooled_narrow",
    "Pre-registered, Wide"   = "flex_attention_weights_pooled_wide"
  )

  # Which parameters the claim is about: b_ are the group-level parameters,
  # r_ the subject-level random effects. Everything else (the random-effect
  # SDs and correlations, lp__, lprior) is left out.
  level_of <- function(variable) case_when(
    str_starts(variable, "b_") ~ "group",
    str_starts(variable, "r_") ~ "subject",
    TRUE                       ~ "not checked"
  )

  # Rhat and the bulk and tail effective sample sizes of every checked
  # parameter of every fit, plus the fit's divergent transitions. The fits of
  # the data are read one at a time and dropped as soon as their diagnostics
  # are out; the simulated-choice fits already carry theirs.
  diags <- list()
  for (nm in names(paper_fits)) {
    file <- file.path(fit_dir, paste0(paper_fits[[nm]], ".rds"))
    if (!file.exists(file)) { cat("No cached fit for", paper_fits[[nm]], "\n"); next }
    fit <- readRDS(file)
    d   <- posterior::summarise_draws(fit, "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail")
    diags[[nm]] <- list(diag = d, divergences = sum(nuts_params(fit, pars = "divergent__")$Value))
    rm(fit); gc()
  }
  for (rng in c("Narrow", "Wide")) {
    files <- list.files(fit_dir, full.names = TRUE,
                        pattern = paste0("^attention_weights_utility_sim_cond_lam_", tolower(rng), "_rep[0-9]+_draws\\.rds$"))
    for (f in files) {
      x  <- readRDS(f)
      nm <- paste0("Simulated choices, ", rng, ", ", str_extract(basename(f), "rep[0-9]+"))
      diags[[nm]] <- list(diag = x$summary, divergences = x$n_divergent)
    }
  }

  # One row per fit and level: the number of parameters, the divergent
  # transitions, the largest Rhat, the smallest effective sample size (bulk or
  # tail) and how many parameters miss either threshold. The parameters that
  # miss one are collected separately.
  conv      <- tibble()
  conv_fail <- tibble()
  for (nm in names(diags)) {
    d <- diags[[nm]]$diag %>%
      mutate(level = level_of(variable)) %>%
      filter(level != "not checked")
    for (lv in c("group", "subject")) {
      x <- d %>% filter(level == lv)
      if (nrow(x) == 0) next
      conv <- bind_rows(conv, tibble(
        model = nm, level = lv, parameters = nrow(x), divergences = diags[[nm]]$divergences,
        max_rhat = max(x$rhat), min_ess = min(c(x$ess_bulk, x$ess_tail)),
        rhat_misses = sum(round(x$rhat, 2) > 1.01),   # Rhat as it would be reported, to two decimals
        ess_misses  = sum(x$ess_bulk <= 1000 | x$ess_tail <= 1000)
      ))
    }
    conv_fail <- bind_rows(conv_fail, d %>%
      filter(round(rhat, 2) > 1.01 | ess_bulk <= 1000 | ess_tail <= 1000) %>%
      mutate(model = nm) %>% select(model, level, variable, rhat, ess_bulk, ess_tail))
  }
  print(conv %>% mutate(max_rhat = round(max_rhat, 4), min_ess = round(min_ess)) %>% as.data.frame())

  # The parameters that miss a threshold, worst Rhat first.
  if (nrow(conv_fail) == 0) {
    cat("No checked parameter misses a threshold.\n")
  } else {
    cat(nrow(conv_fail), "checked parameter(s) miss a threshold:\n")
    print(conv_fail %>% arrange(desc(rhat)) %>% as.data.frame(), digits = 5)
  }

  # The verdict on the two sentences.
  cat(sprintf("No divergent transitions in any model: %s (total %d)\n",
              if (all(conv$divergences == 0)) "PASS" else "FAIL", sum(conv$divergences[!duplicated(conv$model)])))
  cat(sprintf("Rhat < 1.01 (rounded to two decimals) and ESS > 1000 for every group-level parameter and subject-level random effect: %s (largest Rhat %.4f, smallest ESS %.0f)\n",
              if (nrow(conv_fail) == 0) "PASS" else "FAIL", max(conv$max_rhat), min(conv$min_ess)))

  # The snippet: the largest Rhat and the smallest effective sample size over
  # the checked parameters of every fit.
  save_text(sprintf("$\\max \\hat{R} = %.3f$, $\\min \\text{ESS} = %s$",
                    max(conv$max_rhat), gsub(",", "{,}", format(round(min(conv$min_ess)), big.mark = ","))),   # 1{,}011: the comma LaTeX math needs
            "brms_convergence")
}
```
